title: Roots, patterns and root-based dictionaries
text: Lesson overview Level B1 begins with a tool you will use throughout the rest of the course: a dictionary organised by root. In A2, you learnt that almost every Arabic word comes from a root and a pattern (A2-01), and you recognised the derived forms (A2-18). Now you will turn that knowledge into a method: when you encounter an unfamiliar word, even without vowel marks, you will break it down layer by layer, identify its root even if a letter has disappeared or changed, find it in the dictionary and choose the meaning that fits the context. This step will help you work independently with the authentic texts in module B1.3. Two weeks. Item Details Code B1-01 Level B1 · Module B1.1 Systematic Morphology Prerequisites Examination A2 exceeded; root and scheme (A2-01); weak verbs (A2-15, A2-16); derived forms (A2-17, A2-18) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 95–96 of the calendar), plus the EGY track-01 in separate blocks Materials This unit, a dictionary ordered by root (Appendix C), script for speech synthesis, session with the tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. break down a word, even without vowels, into proclitics, prefixes, root with scheme, desinences and pronouns suffixes; 2. categorize the root: healthy, with hamza, doubled, assimilated, concave, defective, doubly weak, four letters; 3. rebuild the root when a letter has fallen, stretched or changed; 4. read a dictionary entry by root: form I with imperfect vowel and maṣdar, forms II.X, names, pluralities and parts thereof; 5. choose between several meanings the one suitable for the context; 6. translate short sentences containing words you are looking for. Two-week plan. In true dictionaries abbreviations are explained in the introduction: read it once, calmly. Root order. The dictionaries per root follow the order of the Arabic alphabet on the first radical, then on the second, then on the third: ⁧ك ت ب⁩ comes before ⁧ك ت م⁩ , which comes before ⁧ك ث ر⁩ . The roots with hamza are searched under the letter ⁧أ⁩ . Bilingual dictionaries. Not all Arabic-Italian dictionaries are sorted by root: some follow the alphabetical order of the entire word. title: The verbal forms I/X
text: Lesson overview In A2 you have combined the forms II and III well (A2-17) and you have learned to recognize the forms IV"X (A2-18). In this unity, you move from recognition to use: you combine all forms, from I to X, in all people and in all ways (perfect, imperfect, conjunctive, juxt, imperative); it forms participles; and maṣdar; learn to predict the meaning of a derivative form from the root. We only work with healthy roots: weak verbs in derived forms are the subject of B1-06. Three weeks. Item Details Code B1-02 Level B1 · Module B1.1 Systematic Morphology Prerequisites B1-01; A2-17, A2-18 Estimated time 15–17 hours · three weeks (weeks 97–99), plus the EGY track in separate blocks Materials This unit, dictionary by root, Grammar G42, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. form perfect, imperfect, imperative, participles and maṣdar the forms of a healthy root; 2. to combine any derived form in all persons, the conjunctive and the juxive; 3. properly vocalize a derived verb written without voice; 4. distinguish union hamza (forms VII, VIII, IX, X) and cutting hamza (form IV); 5. predict the probable meaning of a derived form and verify it in the dictionary; 6. use in context the most frequent derived verbs of the newspaper language. title: The active and passive participle
text: Lesson overview Participle is the most versatile word in Arabic. The same ⁧اسْمُ الفَاعِلِ⁩ (active participle) may be an adjective ('the responsible official'), a name ('the responsible person') almost a verb at present ('I am going'), and holds a complement like a verb; the same applies to ⁧اسْمُ المَفْعُولِ⁩ (passive participle). In the newspapers, participants are everywhere: ⁧المُشَارِكُونَ⁩ , ⁧المُتَّهَمُ⁩ , ⁧المُتَوَقَّعُ⁩ , ⁧المَسْمُوحُ بِهِ⁩ . In this unit you learn to form them from all forms, to recognize active and passive without vowels and to use them in their four roles. Two weeks. Item Details Code B1-03 Level B1 · Module B1.1 Systematic Morphology Prerequisites B1-02 Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 100–101), plus the EGY track Materials This unit, dictionary by root, Grammar G43, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. form the active and passive participle of each form, including the most frequent cases with weak roots; 2. use the participle as an adjective, as a name and with verbal value (present state, imminent action); 3. build the passive participle of verbs with preposition ( ⁧مَسْمُوحٌ بِهِ⁩ , ⁧مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِ⁩ ); 4. form the female and plural participles, healthy and over; 5. to distinguish active and passive participle in a text without vowels thanks to context; 6. translate the participles into English with the most natural form (relative, adjective, name, gerund). Two-week plan. Dialogue 1 · The service of Laylā Video call with Beirut. Laylā prepares a television service on a film festival and tells Luca about his work. Arabic Translation ⁧لُوكَا: مَسَاءُ الخَيْرِ يَا لَيْلَى! تَبْدِينَ مَشْغُولَةً.⁩ Good evening. Laylā! You look busy. ⁧لَيْلَى: مَشْغُولَةٌ جِدًّا! غَدًا يَبْدَأُ مِهْرَجَانُ السِّينَمَا، وَأَنَا المَسْؤُولَةُ عَنِ التَّقْرِيرِ.⁩ Laylā: Very busy! Tomorrow the film festival begins and I am responsible for the service. ⁧لُوكَا: وَمَاذَا سَتُصَوِّرِينَ؟⁩ What are you gonna film? ⁧لَيْلَى: سَأَتَحَدَّثُ مَعَ المُنَظِّمِينَ، وَمَعَ بَعْضِ المُشَارِكِينَ القَادِمِينَ مِنْ عَشْرِ دُوَلٍ. وَمَعَ المُتَطَوِّعِينَ أَيْضًا: أَكْثَرُ مِنْ مِئَتَيْ شَابٍّ وَشَابَّةٍ يَعْمَلُونَ مَجَّانًا.⁩ Laylā: I will talk to the organizers and some participants from ten countries. And also with volunteers: more than 200 boys and girls working for free. ⁧لُوكَا: وَهَلِ الدُّخُولُ مَفْتُوحٌ لِلْجَمِيعِ؟⁩ Luke: And is the entrance open to all? ⁧لَيْلَى: لِلْعُرُوضِ العَامَّةِ نَعَمْ، أَمَّا العُرُوضُ الخَاصَّةُ فَالدُّخُولُ إِلَيْهَا مَسْمُوحٌ بِهِ لِلصَّحَفِيِّينَ المُعْتَمَدِينَ فَقَطْ.⁩ Laylā: For public projections yes; instead, the confidential projections are allowed only to accredited journalists. ⁧لُوكَا: وَأَنْتِ مُعْتَمَدَةٌ طَبْعًا.⁩ Luke: And you are accredited, of course. ⁧المُخْرِجَةُ شَابَّةٌ،⁩ … ⁧طَبْعًا! وَالفِيلْمُ المُنْتَظَرُ هٰذِهِ السَّنَةَ فِيلْمٌ مِصْرِيٌّ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧وَهِيَ مُرَشَّحَةٌ لِلْجَائِزَةِ الأُولَى.⁩ Laylā: Sure! And the most awaited film this year is an Egyptian movie... the director is young and she is nominated for the first prize. ⁧لُوكَا: فِيلْمٌ مِصْرِيٌّ؟ مُمْتَازٌ، سَأُشَاهِدُهُ مَعَ شَرِيف لِأَتَدَرَّبَ عَلَى اللَّهْجَةِ!⁩ An Egyptian movie? Great, I'll look at it with Šarīf to practice my dialect! ⁧المُصَوِّرُ⁩ … ⁧فِكْرَةٌ جَيِّدَةٌ. وَالآنَ اعْذُرْنِي، أَنَا ذَاهِبَةٌ إِلَى اجْتِمَاعٍ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧يَنْتَظِرُنِي!⁩ LaylāGood idea. And now I'm sorry, I'm going to a meeting... the cameraman is waiting for me! What to notice. ⁧المَسْؤُولَةُ عَنْ⁩ The person in charge of the product is a passive participle used as a name. ⁧المُنَظِّمُونَ⁩ , ⁧المُشَارِكُونَ⁩ , ⁧المُتَطَوِّعُونَ⁩ : active parts used as personal names. ⁧القَادِمِينَ مِنْ⁩ • which are derived from: participle with relative value. ⁧مَسْمُوحٌ بِهِ⁩ : passive participle of a preposition verb (section 6). ⁧المُعْتَمَدِينَ⁩ (VIII, ⁧ع م د⁩ ). ⁧المُنْتَظَرُ⁩ Waited. ⁧مُرَشَّحَةٌ⁩ "Candidata" is the name of the company. ⁧ذَاهِبَةٌ⁩ I'm going to go to: Participle with verbal value (section) 5). ⁧المُصَوِّرُ⁩ The photographer, the operator. ⁧اعْذُرْنِي⁩ I'm sorry. ⁧عُرُوض⁩ • screenings, performances (sing. ⁧عَرْض⁩ ). ⁧مِهْرَجَان⁩ Festivals ⁧جَائِزَة⁩ • premium • ⁧مَجَّانًا⁩ Free. 2. When the passive is missing. Intransitional verbs ( ⁧تَطَوَّعَ⁩ , ⁧اِنْسَحَبَ⁩ , ⁧اِسْتَقَلَّ⁩ ) do not have a simple passive participle: they have at most the one with preposition (section 6). 3. Participants of weak roots (recognize) You will study them thoroughly in B1-06; In the meantime, he learns to recognize the most frequent forms. Type Word Active participle Passive participle concave ⁧عَادَ⁩ · ⁧بَاعَ⁩ · ⁧قَالَ⁩ ⁧عَائِد⁩ · ⁧بَائِع⁩ · ⁧قَائِل⁩ ⁧مَبِيع⁩ · ⁧مَقُول⁩ defective · ⁧قَضَى⁩ ⁧قَاضٍدَعَا⁩ ⁧مَقْضِيّالدَّاعِي⁩ / ⁧دَاعٍ⁩ · ⁧القَاضِي⁩ / ⁧مَقْضِيّالدَّاعِي⁩ ⁧مَدْعُوّ⁩ · doubled · ⁧أَحَبَّ⁩ ⁧مُحِبّاِسْتَمَرَّ⁩ · ⁧مُحَبّمُسْتَمِرّ⁩ with hamza ⁧لَجَأَ⁩ · ⁧سَأَلَ⁩ ⁧لَاجِئ⁩ · ⁧سَائِل⁩ ⁧مَسْؤُول⁩ Two rules to remember. 1. In the active participle of form I of concave verbs the weak letter becomes hamza: ⁧قَائِل⁩ , ⁧عَائِد⁩ . 2. The active participle of defects loses the ⁧ي⁩ Without Article: ⁧قَاضٍ⁩ A judge shall be the same, but ⁧القَاضِي⁩ The judge is the judge. 4. The four roles of the participle Role Example Translation adjective ⁧المُوَظَّفُ المَسْؤُولُ عَنِ المَلَفِّ⁩ the official responsible for the practice name ⁧تَحَدَّثَ المَسْؤُولُ إِلَى الصَّحَفِيِّينَ.⁩ The manager spoke to the reporters. almost verb (state, action in progress) ⁧أَنَا ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى المَحَطَّةِ.⁩ I'm going to the station. verb with complement ⁧قَارِئُو الصُّحُفِ⁩ · ⁧المُسَافِرُونَ إِلَى رُومَا⁩ travelers to Rome · readers of newspapers The complement of the participle is built in two ways: with a preposition ( ⁧المُسَافِرُونَ إِلَى رُومَا⁩ ) or iḍāfa ( ⁧قَارِئُو الصُّحُفِ⁩ , ⁧مُسْتَخْدِمُو الإِنْتَرْنِت⁩ ). Iniḍāfa the healthy plural loses the nūn (A2-09). 5. Dialogue 2 · Where are you? Maria phones Luke; They had to meet to study together. Arabic Translation ⁧مَارِيَا: لُوكَا، أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟ أَنَا جَالِسَةٌ فِي المَكْتَبَةِ مُنْذُ نِصْفِ سَاعَةٍ!⁩ Luca, where are you? I've been sitting in the library for half an hour! ⁧لُوكَا: آسِفٌ جِدًّا! أَنَا خَارِجٌ الآنَ مِنَ المَكْتَبِ.⁩ I'm so sorry! I'm leaving the office now. ⁧مَارِيَا: وَهَلْ أَنْتَ قَادِمٌ بِالمِتْرُو؟⁩ And you're coming with the subway? ⁧لُوكَا: لَا، أَنَا رَاكِبٌ الحَافِلَةَ رَقْمَ تِسْعِينَ. أَنَا وَاصِلٌ بَعْدَ عِشْرِينَ دَقِيقَةً.⁩ No, I'm on bus number ninety. I'll be there in 20 minutes. ⁧مَارِيَا: طَيِّبٌ. وَهَلْ أَنْتَ مُسْتَعِدٌّ لِلِامْتِحَانِ؟⁩ Okay. And you're ready for the test? ⁧هَلْ أَنْتِ فَاهِمَةٌ دَرْسَ الأَوْزَانِ؟⁩ … ⁧لَسْتُ مُتَأَكِّدًا⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luca: I'm not sure... Did you understand the lesson about forms? ⁧مَارِيَا: نَعَمْ، وَأَنَا مُحْضِرَةٌ مَعِي جَدْوَلًا كَامِلًا.⁩ Maria: Yes, and I brought with me a complete table. ⁧لُوكَا: أَنْتِ رَائِعَةٌ! أَنَا مَدِينٌ لَكِ بِقَهْوَةٍ.⁩ You're amazing! I owe you a coffee. ⁧بَلْ بِقَهْوَتَيْنِ: وَاحِدَةٍ لِلتَّأَخُّرِ، وَوَاحِدَةٍ لِلْجَدْوَلِ!⁩ : ⁧مَارِيَا⁩ In fact, two coffees: one for the delay and one for the table! What to notice. In this dialogue, the participants do the work of the Italian verbs: ⁧جَالِسَةٌ⁩ The following paragraph is added: ⁧خَارِجٌ⁩ I'm going out. ⁧قَادِمٌ⁩ You're coming. ⁧رَاكِبٌ الحَافِلَةَ⁩ They are on the bus (with direct complement!), ⁧وَاصِلٌ بَعْدَ⁩ ... ... . ...Arrival between... ⁧فَاهِمَةٌ⁩ You know, you're one who understands. ⁧مُحْضِرَةٌ⁩ I have brought ⁧مَدِينٌ لَكِ بِـ⁩ I owe you (Lett. I'm liable to you for that. 6. Participle as a verb: what time does it express? The participle does not have its own time: it expresses a state or action seen in its course or outcome. The Italian translation depends on the verb. Type of verb Participle value Example motion ongoing or imminent action ⁧نَحْنُ مُسَافِرُونَ غَدًا⁩ · ⁧أَنَا ذَاهِبٌ⁩ position present status ⁧هِيَ وَاقِفَةٌ⁩ · ⁧هُوَ جَالِسٌ⁩ perception, knowledge resulting status ⁧هَلْ أَنْتَ عَارِفٌ الطَّرِيقَ؟⁩ · ⁧أَنَا فَاهِمٌ⁩ Action taken present result ⁧هِيَ مُحْضِرَةٌ الأَوْرَاقَ⁩ He brought the documents (and he has them with him) In the formal written language this verbal use is less frequent than in the spoken language: in newspapers the participle appears mainly as an adjective and as a name. In the spoken language, and in the Egyptian, it is very frequent (A2-23: ʿāyiz, sākin, fāhim). 7. The passive participle with preposition If the verb holds a preposition ( ⁧سَمَحَ بِـ⁩ , ⁧اِتَّفَقَ عَلَى⁩ , ⁧شَكَّ فِي⁩ ), the passive participle is invariant and carries the preposition with a pronoun that accords with the name. Word Participle with preposition Example ⁧سَمَحَ بِـ⁩ • Allow • • ⁧بِهَا⁩ / ⁧مَسْمُوحٌ بِهِ⁩ ⁧السُّرْعَةُ المَسْمُوحُ بِهَا⁩ The permissible speed of the vehicle shall be: ⁧اِتَّفَقَ عَلَى⁩ • Agreed on •  The agreed appointment is ⁧المَوْعِدُ المُتَّفَقُ عَلَيْهِمُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِ⁩ ⁧شَكَّ فِي⁩ Doubtful of  ⁧خَبَرٌ مَشْكُوكٌ فِيهِمَشْكُوكٌ فِيهِ⁩ • a dubious news • ⁧رَغِبَ فِي⁩ Wish you wish.  ⁧غَيْرُ مَرْغُوبٍ فِيهِمَرْغُوبٌ فِيهِ⁩ Undesirable effects ⁧اِشْتَبَهَ فِي⁩ • suspecting of • ⁧المُشْتَبَهُ بِهِفِيهِ⁩ / ⁧مُشْتَبَهٌ بِهِ⁩ The suspect is the suspect (A2-20) The deal. The participle remains to the singular male; only the pronoun is agreed: ⁧الكَمِّيَّةُ المَسْمُوحُ بِهَا⁩ • the quantity allowed • • ⁧الأَشْخَاصُ المُشْتَبَهُ بِهِمْ⁩ • the persons suspected. 8. Female and plural Participium Feminine Healthy Plural Plural over frequent  ⁧كَاتِبُونَكَاتِبَةكَاتِب⁩ (adjective) ⁧كُتَّاب⁩ • Writers  ⁧طَالِبَةطَالِب⁩ — ⁧طُلَّاب⁩  ⁧عَامِلُونَعَامِلَةعَامِل⁩ Working ⁧عُمَّال⁩ Workers  ⁧سَاكِنَةسَاكِن⁩ — ⁧سُكَّان⁩ Inhabitants  ⁧قَائِدَةقَائِد⁩ — ⁧قَادَة⁩ • Heads, executives   ⁧مُشَارِكُونَمُشَارِكَةمُشَارِك⁩ — ⁧مَشْرُوع⁩ — ⁧مَشَارِيعُمَشْرُوعَات⁩ • projects • ⁧مَوْضُوع⁩ — ⁧مَوَاضِيعُمَوْضُوعَات⁩ Subject matter Practical rules. Participles of derived forms ( ⁧مُـ⁩ ) they almost always take the healthy plural: ⁧مُوَظَّفُونَ⁩ , ⁧مُتَطَوِّعُونَ⁩ . Participants of Form Used as trade or category names often have a plural over ( ⁧كُتَّاب⁩ , ⁧عُمَّال⁩ , ⁧تُجَّار⁩ ); used as adjectives, the healthy plural. The passive participles referring to things take ⁧ـات⁩ or a plural over ( ⁧مَشَارِيعُ⁩ ). 9. Active or passive without vowels? In active and passive derived forms the same are written: ⁧مرسل⁩ , ⁧مستقبل⁩ , ⁧محتل⁩ , ⁧منظم⁩ . Decide with three questions: 1. Person or what? A person doing the action → active: ⁧المُنَظِّمُونَ⁩ The organisers are the organizers. Something that suffer → passive: ⁧مَعْرِضٌ مُنَظَّمٌ جَيِّدًا⁩ It's a well-organized exhibition. 2. Is there a complement? A direct or in iḍāfa → Active: ⁧مُرْسِلُ الرِّسَالَةِ⁩ The sender of the letter is the same as the sender. 3. What does the rest of the sentence say? ⁧المُسْتَقْبَلُ القَرِيبُ⁩ • the near future (passive, fixed) · ⁧المُسْتَقْبِلُونَ⁩ Those receiving (asset). Watch out for the couples in the news. ⁧المُتَّهَمُ⁩ The defendant, the accused (passive) / ⁧المُتَّهِمُ⁩ • the accuser (active, rare); ⁧الأَرَاضِي المُحْتَلَّةُ⁩ The occupied territories (passive) / ⁧المُحْتَلُّ⁩ • the overweight (active). A vowel changes who does and who suffers: in a translation it is a serious mistake. 10. Pronunciation I'm the decisive one. Try to pronounce the couples clearly: munaẓẓim / munaẓẓam, mursil / mursal, mustaqbil / mustaqbal. The tutor says one of the two words, you say whether it's active or passive. The concave hamza. qāʾil, ʿāʾid, bāʾiʿ: the hamza between the two vowels must be pronounced, with a small detachment, not as a y (*qāyil is Egyptian, not fuṣḥā). 11. title: The maṣdar
text: Lesson overview The maṣdar ( ⁧المَصْدَر⁩ , "source" is the name of action: ⁧زَارَ⁩ • visited • • ⁧زِيَارَة⁩ The visit, the visit. You've known him since A2 as a single word; a B1 It becomes a construction. The language of newspapers, laws and public notices prefers the maṣdar to the verb: The Minister's visit to Cairo instead of the Minister's visit to Cairo is necessary,  the reservation is required instead of the reservation must be made. Who can't take down a chain of maṣdar He doesn't understand a newspaper headline. In this unity learn the forms of maṣdar, how it holds subject and complements and how it replaces subordinate phrases. Two weeks. Item Details Code B1-04 Level B1 · Module B1.1 Systematic Morphology Prerequisites B1-02, B1-03 Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 102–103), plus the EGY track Materials This unit, dictionary by root, Grammar G44, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. Recognize the main patterns of maṣdar form I and find them in the dictionary; 2. to safely form the maṣdar For the purposes of this Regulation, the following definitions apply: 3. use the maṣdar in place of ⁧أَنْ⁩ + verb; 4. build the maṣdar with its subject and its complement ( ⁧زِيَارَةُ الوَزِيرِ لِلْقَاهِرَةِ⁩ ); 5. use preposition + maṣdar instead of a subordinate sentence ( ⁧بَعْدَ وُصُولِهِ⁩ , ⁧مِنْ أَجْلِ الحُصُولِ عَلَى⁩ …) e deny with ⁧عَدَم⁩ ; 6. form abstract names in ⁧ـِيَّة⁩ and read notices and titles built with the maṣdar. title: The passive
text: Lesson overview The Arab passive is invisible: ⁧كتب⁩ may be ⁧كَتَبَ⁩ It has written: ⁧كُتِبَ⁩ It has been written, and the difference lies in the vowels that the newspapers do not write. Yet passiveness is everywhere in the language of information: ⁧يُقَالُ إِنَّ⁩ It is said that, ⁧يُعْتَقَدُ أَنَّ⁩ ... it is considered that, ⁧عُثِرَ عَلَى⁩ It has been found to be in the form of: ⁧تَمَّ افْتِتَاحُ⁩ It has been inaugurated. In this unit you learn to form the internal passive of all forms, to recognize it without vowels, to use alternative newspaper constructions ( ⁧تَمَّ⁩ + maṣdar) and to translate it into English naturally. Two weeks. Item Details Code B1-05 Level B1 · Module B1.1 Systematic Morphology Prerequisites B1-02, B1-03, B1-04 Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 104–105), plus the EGY track Materials This unit, dictionary by root, Grammar G45, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. form the passive internal to perfect and imperfect, in form I and derived forms; 2. grant the passive verb with its subject ( ⁧نَائِبُ الفَاعِلِ⁩ ); 3. recognize the passive in a text without vowels thanks to context; 4. recognizing the most frequent passives of weak verbs ( ⁧قِيلَ⁩ , ⁧يُقَالُ⁩ , ⁧وُجِدَ⁩ , ⁧يُوجَدُ⁩ , ⁧وُلِدَ⁩ , ⁧تُوُفِّيَ⁩ ); 5. use impersonal liabilities and fixed expressions ( ⁧يُسْمَحُ بِـ⁩ , ⁧يُقَالُ إِنَّ⁩ , ⁧يُعَدُّ⁩ ); 6. use and translate constructions with ⁧تَمَّ⁩ and ⁧جَرَى⁩ + maṣdar and the staff member, ⁧مِنْ قِبَلِ.⁩ Two-week plan. Dialogue 1 · A discovery at Luxor Luca and Karīm They read a piece of news together on an Arabic website. Arabic Translation ⁧اُكْتُشِفَتْ مَقْبَرَةٌ فِرْعَوْنِيَّةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ قُرْبَ⁩ » ⁧هَلْ قَرَأْتَ هٰذَا الخَبَرَ؟⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ .« ⁧الأُقْصُرِ⁩ Karīm: Have you read this news? A new pharaonic tomb near Luxor has been discovered. ⁧لُوكَا: اُكْتُشِفَتْ؟ لِمَاذَا الضَّمَّةُ؟⁩ Luke: "Is it discovered"? Why the u? ⁧كَرِيم: لِأَنَّ الفِعْلَ مَبْنِيٌّ لِلْمَجْهُولِ: لَا نَعْرِفُ مَنِ اكْتَشَفَهَا، أَوْ لَا يُهِمُّ.⁩ Karīm: Because the verb is passive: we don't know who discovered it, or it doesn't matter. ⁧مِنْ قِبَلِ فَرِيقٍ مِنْ عُلَمَاءِ الآثَارِ⁩ » ⁧لٰكِنَّ الخَبَرَ يَقُولُ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ:⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ .« ⁧المِصْرِيِّينَ⁩ Luke: But the news then says: "by a team of Egyptian archaeologists." ⁧فِي⁩ .« ⁧مِنْ قِبَلِ⁩ » ⁧نَعَمْ، الصُّحُفُ الحَدِيثَةُ تَذْكُرُ الفَاعِلَ أَحْيَانًا بِـ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧العَرَبِيَّةِ القَدِيمَةِ هٰذَا نَادِرٌ جِدًّا.⁩ Karīm: Yes, modern newspapers sometimes indicate the agent with In ancient Arabic it is very rare. .« ⁧وَقَدْ عُثِرَ دَاخِلَ المَقْبَرَةِ عَلَى تَمَاثِيلَ صَغِيرَةٍ⁩ » ⁧وَهُنَا:⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luke: And here: "Inside the tomb small statues have been found. ⁧كَرِيم: عُثِرَ عَلَى يَعْنِي وُجِدَ. فِعْلٌ مَجْهُولٌ مَعَ حَرْفِ جَرٍّ، وَلِهٰذَا لَا يَتَغَيَّرُ.⁩ Karīm: «ʿuṯira ʿalā• • means • • •wuǧida”, “was found”. It is a passive verb with preposition, and for this it does not change. ⁧وَمِنَ المُتَوَقَّعِ أَنْ يَتِمَّ افْتِتَاحُ المَقْبَرَةِ لِلزُّوَّارِ العَامَ⁩ » ⁧وَهٰذِهِ الجُمْلَةُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ .« ⁧القَادِمَ⁩ Luca: And this sentence? The tomb is expected to be opened to visitors next year. « ⁧تَمَّ⁩ » ⁧الصَّحَفِيُّونَ يُحِبُّونَ⁩ .« ⁧تُفْتَتَحَ⁩ » ⁧يَعْنِي⁩ « ⁧يَتِمَّ افْتِتَاحُ⁩ » ⁧كَرِيم:⁩ ⁧الَّتِي لَا يَكْتُبُهَا أَحَدٌ!⁩ … ⁧لِأَنَّهَا أَوْضَحُ مِنَ الضَّمَّةِ⁩ « ⁧يَتِمُّ⁩ » ⁧وَ⁩ Karīm: "Avvenga l'apertura" means "aperto" (open) " . Journalists love \'tammaÂ' and \'yatimmu' because they are clearer than the u... that no one writes! ⁧يُمْكِنُ أَنْ تَكُونَ كَتَبَ أَوْ كُتِبَ.⁩ « ⁧كتب⁩ » ⁧صَحِيحٌ. بِدُونِ حَرَكَاتٍ،⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ It's true. Without vowels, the word "ktb" may be spelled "------------------------------------------------------------------------ ⁧كَرِيم: لِهٰذَا السِّيَاقُ مُهِمٌّ: إِذَا لَمْ تَجِدْ فَاعِلًا، فَكِّرْ فِي المَجْهُولِ.⁩ Karīm: For this reason the context is important: if you don't find a person who does the action, think about the passive. ⁧أَيْضًا مَجْهُولٌ، صَحِيحٌ؟ وَلَدَتْ مَرْيَمُ، أُخْتُ هُدَى، ابْنَهَا⁩ « ⁧وُلِدَ⁩ » ⁧وَ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧وَوُلِدَ آدَمُ فِي الصَّيْفِ.⁩ … ⁧آدَمَ فِي الصَّيْفِ⁩ Luke: And he was born too, is passive, right? Maryam, the sister of Hudā, gave birth to his son Ādam in the summer... and Ādam was born in the summer. ⁧بِالضَّبْطِ! مِثَالٌ مُمْتَازٌ.⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ Karīm: Exactly! Good example. What to notice. ⁧اُكْتُشِفَتْ⁩ It has been discovered: passive form VIII, with u in the first syllables and before the last radical. ⁧المَبْنِيُّ لِلْمَجْهُولِ⁩ Built for the unknown: the Arabic name of the passive. ⁧مِنْ قِبَلِ⁩ . ⁧عُثِرَ عَلَى⁩ : Impersonal liabilities (section 7). ⁧يَتِمَّ افْتِتَاحُ⁩ : construction with ⁧تَمَّ⁩ (Section 8). ⁧وُلِدَ⁩ - was born: in Arabic, is the liability of ⁧وَلَدَ⁩ • to give birth. ⁧عُلَمَاءُ الآثَارِ⁩ The archaeologists (Lett. The scholars of antiquities. ⁧الضَّمَّة⁩ The vowel is the voice of the vowel. ⁧حَرْفُ جَرٍّ⁩ "Preposition" is given. ⁧نَادِر⁩ Rare. 2. What is the Arab passive The Arab passive is used when the person who performs the action is unknown, obvious or not interested. That's why the Arabic grammar calls it ⁧المَبْنِيُّ لِلْمَجْهُولِ⁩ . The name that undergoes the action becomes the grammatical subject and goes to the name: it is called ⁧نَائِبُ الفَاعِلِ⁩ , is the substitute for the subject. Assets Liabilities Translation ⁧كَتَبَ الطَّالِبُ الرِّسَالَةَ.⁩ ⁧كُتِبَتِ الرِّسَالَةُ.⁩ The letter was written. ⁧فَتَحَ المُوَظَّفُ البَابَ.⁩ ⁧فُتِحَ البَابُ.⁩ The door was opened. ⁧يَسْتَخْدِمُ النَّاسُ هٰذِهِ الكَلِمَةَ.⁩ ⁧تُسْتَخْدَمُ هٰذِهِ الكَلِمَةُ.⁩ This word is used. The agent is normally not here. In classical Arabic the passive and the agent are excluded: if you know who did the action, use the asset. The modern language, under the influence of European languages, sometimes adds the agent with ⁧مِنْ قِبَلِ⁩ (Section 9). 3. The forms of internal liabilities The passive forms by changing the vowels, without adding letters. The rule. Perfect: u in the first syllable (and in all syllables before the last radical), before the last radical. Imperfect: prefix with u, before the last radical. Form Perfect Active Perfect liabilities Imperfect activity Imperfect liability I   ⁧يُكْتَبُيَكْتُبُكُتِبَكَتَبَ⁩  II   ⁧يُنَظَّمُيُنَظِّمُنُظِّمَنَظَّمَ⁩  III   ⁧يُنَاقَشُيُنَاقِشُنُوقِشَنَاقَشَ⁩  IV   ⁧يُرْسَلُيُرْسِلُأُرْسِلَأَرْسَلَ⁩  VIII   ⁧يُنْتَخَبُيَنْتَخِبُاُنْتُخِبَاِنْتَخَبَ⁩  X   ⁧يُسْتَخْدَمُيَسْتَخْدِمُاُسْتُخْدِمَاِسْتَخْدَمَ⁩  Comments. 1. In form III ā becomes ū: ⁧نَاقَشَ⁩ → ⁧نُوقِشَ⁩ . 2. In forms IV and II, the passive imperfect is distinguished from the active only for vowel before the last radical: ⁧يُرْسِلُ⁩ ... ⁧يُرْسَلُ⁩ It shall be sent. 3. Form VII has no passive value: it already has a passive or reflective value ( ⁧اِنْكَسَرَ⁩ It's broken. Forms V and VI have a rare passive, which you just recognize. 4. The passive unites in all people like the asset: ⁧كُتِبْتُ⁩ , ⁧كُتِبُوا⁩ , ⁧يُكْتَبُونَ⁩ ; to the conjunctive and juxtaposed: ⁧أَنْ يُكْتَبَ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يُكْتَبْ.⁩ 4. The Agreement The passive verb agrees with its subject ( ⁧نَائِبُ الفَاعِلِ⁩ ) as an active verb with its subject: to the singular if it precedes (A2), generally and number if followed. Example Translation ⁧كُتِبَ التَّقْرِيرُ.⁩ The report was written. Example Translation ⁧كُتِبَتِ الرِّسَالَةُ.⁩ The letter was written. ⁧أُرْسِلَتِ الطُّرُودُ أَمْسِ.⁩ The packages were shipped yesterday. ⁧اُنْتُخِبَ ثَلَاثَةُ أَعْضَاءٍ جُدُدٍ.⁩ Three new members were elected. ⁧الطُّلَّابُ دُعُوا إِلَى الاِجْتِمَاعِ.⁩ Students were invited to the meeting. ⁧الطُّرُود⁩ • the packages (sing. ⁧طَرْد⁩ ) · ⁧أَعْضَاء⁩ (sing. ⁧عُضْو⁩ ). Subject goes to name. ⁧فُتِحَ البَابُ⁩ , ⁧البَابَ⁩ : what in the asset was the object complement is now subject. In the vociferous texts this is a valuable clue. 5. Dialogue 2 · A late movie Laylā Call Luca from the Beirut festival. Arabic Translation ⁧لَيْلَى: لُوكَا! لَنْ تُصَدِّقَ مَا حَدَثَ. أُجِّلَ عَرْضُ الفِيلْمِ المِصْرِيِّ!⁩ LaylāLuca! You're not gonna believe this. The screening of the Egyptian film has been postponed! ⁧لُوكَا: أُجِّلَ؟ لِمَاذَا؟⁩ - Sent back? Why? ⁧لَيْلَى: قِيلَ لَنَا إِنَّ نُسْخَةَ الفِيلْمِ لَمْ تَصِلْ مِنَ القَاهِرَةِ. يَبْدُو أَنَّهَا أُرْسِلَتْ إِلَى عُنْوَانٍ خَاطِئٍ!⁩ Laylā: We are told that the copy of the film did not come from Cairo. Looks like it was sent to a wrong address! ⁧لُوكَا: يَا لَلْمُصِيبَةِ! وَمَاذَا حَدَثَ لِلْجُمْهُورِ؟⁩ What a disaster! And what happened to the public? ⁧لَيْلَى: دُعِيَ الجُمْهُورُ إِلَى مُشَاهَدَةِ فِيلْمٍ آخَرَ، وَأُعِيدَتِ النُّقُودُ لِمَنْ لَمْ يُرِدِ البَقَاءَ.⁩ Laylā: The audience was invited to see another movie, and the money was returned to those who did not want to stay. ⁧لُوكَا: وَمَتَى سَيُعْرَضُ الفِيلْمُ؟⁩ Luca: And when will the film be screened? ⁧لَيْلَى: لَمْ يُحَدَّدْ مَوْعِدٌ جَدِيدٌ بَعْدُ. يُقَالُ إِنَّهُ سَيُعْرَضُ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ، لٰكِنْ لَمْ يُعْلَنْ ذٰلِكَ رَسْمِيًّا.⁩ Laylā: A new date has not yet been set. It is said that it will be screened on Saturday, but it has not been officially announced. ⁧لُوكَا: وَهَلْ سَتَكْتُبِينَ عَنْ هٰذَا فِي تَقْرِيرِكِ؟⁩ Luke: And will you write about it in your service? ⁧تَأْجِيلُ عَرْضِ الفِيلْمِ⁩ » ⁧طَبْعًا! هٰذَا هُوَ الخَبَرُ الحَقِيقِيُّ اليَوْمَ:⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ .« ⁧المُنْتَظَرِ بِسَبَبِ خَطَأٍ فِي الشَّحْنِ⁩ Laylā: Sure! This is the real news of today:         \ Posted the projection of the film expected for an error of shipment Â . ⁧بِالمَصْدَرِ!⁩ … ⁧عُنْوَانٌ مُمْتَازٌ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luca: Excellent title ... with the maṣdar! ⁧يَبْدُو أَنَّ سَلْمَى عَلَّمَتْكَ جَيِّدًا.⁩ ( ⁧تَضْحَكُ⁩ ) ⁧لَيْلَى:⁩ Laylā: (laughs) You can see that Salmā He taught you well. What to notice. Eight passive in a dialogue: ⁧أُجِّلَ⁩ (II), ⁧قِيلَ⁩ (concave), ⁧أُرْسِلَتْ⁩ (IV), ⁧دُعِيَ⁩ (bad), ⁧أُعِيدَتْ⁩ (IV concave), ⁧سَيُعْرَضُ⁩ (I, future), ⁧لَمْ يُحَدَّدْ⁩ (II, Judging) ⁧لَمْ يُعْلَنْ⁩ (IV, Judging). ⁧قِيلَ لَنَا إِنَّ⁩ We are told that: ⁧قَالَ⁩ and its derivatives are used ⁧إِنَّ⁩ , ⁧أَنَّ. يَا لَلْمُصِيبَةِ⁩ This is a disaster. ⁧بَعْدُ⁩ at the end of a negative sentence: 6. Recognizing the passive without vowels Four clues, to use together. 1. There is no agent, and the name after the verb is something that suffers. ⁧أرسلت الطرود⁩ : packages not ship, are shipped → ⁧أُرْسِلَتِ الطُّرُودُ.⁩ 2. The verb is at the beginning of a news, followed by a name of what and a complement of time or place. ⁧افتتح المعرض أمس⁩ → ⁧اُفْتُتِحَ المَعْرِضُ أَمْسِ⁩ The exhibition was inaugurated yesterday. 3. C'è ⁧مِنْ قِبَلِ⁩ , ⁧عَلَى يَدِ⁩ , ⁧مِنْ طَرَفِ⁩ : The agent is introduced by a preposition, so the verb is passive. 4. It is a fixed expression: ⁧يقال إن⁩ , ⁧يعتقد أن⁩ , ⁧يذكر أن⁩ , ⁧يرجى⁩ , ⁧يمنع⁩ , ⁧يوجد⁩ , ⁧يعد⁩ . These must be recognized as I'll be right there. Attention to the first person. ⁧كتبت⁩ may be ⁧كَتَبْتُ⁩ I wrote it down. ⁧كَتَبْتَ⁩ You wrote it. ⁧كَتَبَتْ⁩ She wrote and also ⁧كُتِبَتْ⁩ It has been written. The context (who speaks? is there an object?) decides. 7. The passives of weak verbs (recognize) Type Assets Perfect liabilities Imperfect liability concava I  ⁧يُقَالُقِيلَقَالَ⁩  concava I  ⁧يُبَاعُبِيعَبَاعَ⁩  concave IV  ⁧يُقَامُأُقِيمَأَقَامَ⁩  concave VIII  ⁧يُخْتَارُاُخْتِيرَاِخْتَارَ⁩  defect I  ⁧دُعِيَدَعَا⁩ ⁧يُدْعَى⁩ defect IV  ⁧أُلْغِيَأَلْغَى⁩ ⁧يُلْغَى⁩ assimilated I  ⁧يُوجَدُوُجِدَوَجَدَ⁩  assimilated I  ⁧يُولَدُوُلِدَوَلَدَ⁩  doubled I ⁧يُعَدُّعُدَّعَدَّ⁩ Three words that you already know and are passive. ⁧يُوجَدُ⁩ The liabilities of ⁧وَجَدَ⁩ : literally “is located”. ⁧وُلِدَ⁩ - is the liability of ⁧وَلَدَ⁩ • to give birth. ⁧تُوُفِّيَ⁩ - has died, has died, is the liability of ⁧تَوَفَّى⁩ (V), because in the traditional vision it is God who takes to himself the soul: the most respectful word for the death of a person, that of obituaries and news. ⁧يُعَدُّ⁩ It is considered to be . Frequent in the newspapers: ⁧يُعَدُّ هٰذَا المَتْحَفُ مِنْ أَهَمِّ المَتَاحِفِ فِي العَالَمِ⁩ This museum is considered one of the most important in the world. 8. title: Weak verbs in derived forms
text: Lesson overview In A2 you have learned the weak verbs of form I ( ⁧قَالَ⁩ , ⁧مَشَى⁩ , ⁧وَصَلَ⁩ , ⁧ظَنَّ⁩ ). In derived forms the same roots produce some of the most frequent verbs of the written language: ⁧أَقَامَ⁩ , ⁧اِخْتَارَ⁩ , ⁧اِسْتَفَادَ⁩ , ⁧اِنْتَهَى⁩ , ⁧أَلْغَى⁩ , ⁧أَدَّى⁩ , ⁧اِتَّصَلَ⁩ , ⁧اِسْتَمَرَّ⁩ . Their forms are missing from a letter, and those who do not know how to reconstruct it do not find the root in the dictionary and do not recognize the verb in the sentence. In this unit you tidy up the system: for each type of weak root see what happens in every form, with conjugation, the maṣdar And the participants. Three weeks. Item Details Code B1-06 Level B1 · Module B1.1 Systematic Morphology Prerequisites B1-02 … B1-05; weak verbs of form I (A2) Estimated time 18–20 hours · three weeks (weeks 106–108), plus the EGY track Materials This unit, dictionary by root, Grammar G46, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. to recognize in which forms each type of weak root behaves irregularly; 2. Conjugate concave verbs of forms IV, VII, VIII and X ( ⁧أَقَامَ⁩ , ⁧اِخْتَارَ⁩ , ⁧اِسْتَفَادَ⁩ ); 3. to combine the defective verbs of all forms ( ⁧أَدَّى⁩ , ⁧عَانَى⁩ , ⁧أَلْغَى⁩ , ⁧تَحَدَّى⁩ , ⁧اِنْتَهَى⁩ , ⁧اِسْتَدْعَى⁩ ); 4. recognizing assimilation in form VIII ( ⁧اِتَّصَلَ⁩ , ⁧اِتَّفَقَ⁩ ) and the forms of verbs doubled ( ⁧اِسْتَمَرَّ⁩ , ⁧اِسْتَمْرَرْتُ⁩ ); 5. form maṣdar and parts of all these verbs; 6. go back to the root from any form and find it in the dictionary. The juxtaposed loses the long vowel: ⁧لَمْ يَنْتَهِ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَتَحَدَّ⁩ . 4. In front of a suffix that begins with a consonant reappears the ⁧ي⁩ : ⁧أَلْغَيْتُ⁩ , ⁧اِنْتَهَيْنَا⁩ , ⁧تَحَدَّيْتُمْ⁩ . 5. title: Names of place, time and instrument
text: Lesson overview ⁧مَكْتَب⁩ , ⁧مَطْبَخ⁩ , ⁧مَدْرَسَة⁩ , ⁧مِفْتَاح⁩ , ⁧مُسْتَشْفًى⁩ : You've known them for a long time as single words. They are actually built with few fixed patterns: ⁧مَفْعَل⁩ and ⁧مَفْعِل⁩ for places and times, ⁧مِفْعَال⁩ and ⁧مِفْعَلَة⁩ for instruments, the passive participle for places of derived forms. Knowing the patterns allows you to understand new words at the first meeting ( ⁧مَخْبَز⁩ From the root          'Cooking bread is the bakery) and to find in the dictionary the words that begin to ⁧مَـ⁩ and ⁧مِـ⁩ . It's the last unit on the module. B1.1. A week. Item Details Code B1-07 Level B1 · Module B1.1 Systematic Morphology Prerequisites B1-01 … B1-06 Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 109), plus the EGY track Materials This unit, dictionary by root, Grammar G47, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognize and form the names of place and time of form I ( ⁧مَفْعَل⁩ , ⁧مَفْعِل⁩ , ⁧مَفْعَلَة⁩ ); 2. form their plural ( ⁧مَفَاعِل⁩ ); 3. recognizing the place names of weak roots and derived forms ( ⁧مَبْنًى⁩ , ⁧مَحَلّ⁩ , ⁧مُسْتَشْفًى⁩ , ⁧مُلْتَقًى⁩ ); 4. recognizing and forming instrument names ( ⁧مِفْعَل⁩ , ⁧مِفْعَال⁩ , ⁧مِفْعَلَة⁩ ) and modern instruments in ⁧فَعَّالَة⁩ ; 5. deduce the meaning of a new word from root and scheme, and verify it in the dictionary. Plan of the week. title: Word phrases and nominal sentence: order and agreement
text: Lesson overview With the module B1.2 from the word to the sentence. The first question is simple only in appearance: in what order are subject and verb put, and how do they agree? In Arabic the answer changes according to order: ⁧وَصَلَ الوُزَرَاءُ⁩ The ministers have arrived, and the verb to the singular, ⁧الوُزَرَاءُ وَصَلُوا⁩ has the verb in plural. Newspapers write headlines under the first name ( ⁧الحُكُومَةُ تَرْفَعُ الأُجُورَ⁩ ) and the text with the verb before ( ⁧رَفَعَتِ الحُكُومَةُ الأُجُورَ⁩ ). And the plurals of things want the singular feminine: ⁧السَّيَّارَاتُ وَصَلَتْ⁩ . In this unit you put in order all these rules, which you met to pieces in A1 and A2. Two weeks. Item Details Code B1-08 Level B1 · Module B1.2 ... Prerequisites Module B1.1 exceeded Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 111–112), plus the EGY track Materials This unit, Grammar G48, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. distinguish the verbal phrase ( ⁧الجُمْلَةُ الفِعْلِيَّةُ⁩ ) from the nominal sentence ( ⁧الجُمْلَةُ الاِسْمِيَّةُ⁩ ) and move from one to the other; 2. grant the verb with the subject when he precedes it and when he follows it; 3. to give verbs, adjectives and pronouns with plural things (singular feminine); 4. build sentences with an indefinite subject ( ⁧فِي المَكْتَبِ رَجُلٌ⁩ , ⁧عِنْدِي سُؤَالٌ⁩ ); 5. recognize the nominal titles and the verbal text of the articles, and the order with the pronomial complement ( ⁧زَارَنِي⁩ ⁧صَدِيقٌ⁩ ); 6. accord the verb with the coordinated subjects and collective names. Two-week plan. Dialogue 1 · The title and text Video call with Beirut. Luke asks Laylā because newspaper headlines have a different order than text. Arabic Translation ⁧الحُكُومَةُ⁩ » ⁧فِي العُنْوَانِ تَكْتُبُونَ:⁩ .« ⁧صَحَفِيٌّ⁩ » ⁧لَيْلَى، عِنْدِي سُؤَالٌ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧لِمَاذَا؟⁩ .« ⁧رَفَعَتِ الحُكُومَةُ الأُجُورَ⁩ » : ⁧، وَفِي النَّصِّ⁩ « ⁧تَرْفَعُ الأُجُورَ⁩ Luca: Laylā, I have a question of the journalism. In the title, write "The government increases wages" and in the text "It has increased government wages." Why? ⁧لَيْلَى: سُؤَالٌ ذَكِيٌّ! فِي العُنْوَانِ نَبْدَأُ بِالاِسْمِ، لِأَنَّ القَارِئَ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَعْرِفَ فَوْرًا مَنْ فَعَلَ. وَفِي النَّصِّ نَعُودُ إِلَى الجُمْلَةِ الفِعْلِيَّةِ، وَهِيَ الأَكْثَرُ طَبِيعِيَّةً فِي العَرَبِيَّةِ.⁩ Laylā: Smart question! In the title we begin with the name, because the reader wants to know immediately who acted. In the text we return to the verbal phrase, which is the most natural in Arabic. ⁧الوُزَرَاءُ⁩ » ⁧بِالمُفْرَدِ، وَلٰكِنْ⁩ « ⁧وَصَلَ الوُزَرَاءُ⁩ » ⁧وَلَاحَظْتُ شَيْئًا آخَرَ:⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ . ⁧بِالجَمْعِ⁩ « ⁧وَصَلُوا⁩ Luke: And I noticed another thing: "The ministers arrived, with the singular, but the ministers arrived, with the plural. ⁧لَيْلَى: صَحِيحٌ. إِذَا جَاءَ الفِعْلُ قَبْلَ الفَاعِلِ، يَبْقَى مُفْرَدًا. وَإِذَا جَاءَ بَعْدَهُ، يُطَابِقُهُ فِي العَدَدِ.⁩ Laylā: Right. If the verb comes before the subject, it remains to the singular. If he comes later, he'll settle with him in the number. ⁧لُوكَا: وَالجِنْسُ؟⁩ What about the genre? ⁧أَمَّا جَمْعُ غَيْرِ العَاقِلِ،⁩ .« ⁧وَصَلَتِ الوَزِيرَاتُ⁩ » ⁧الجِنْسُ يَتَغَيَّرُ دَائِمًا:⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧، دَائِمًا⁩ « ⁧الطَّائِرَاتُ وَصَلَتْ⁩ » ⁧،⁩ « ⁧وَصَلَتِ الطَّائِرَاتُ⁩ » ⁧فَلَهُ قَاعِدَةٌ خَاصَّةٌ:⁩ ⁧مُؤَنَّثٌ مُفْرَدٌ.⁩ Laylā: The genre always changes: the ministre have arrived. The plural of non-humans, on the other hand, has its own rule: "the planes have arrived," always in the singular female, before or after. ⁧؟⁩ « ⁧الكُتُبُ جَدِيدَةٌ⁩ » ⁧حَتَّى⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luke: Are books new too? ⁧الكُتُبُ جَدِيدَةٌ، وَالقَرَارَاتُ مُهِمَّةٌ، وَالأَسْعَارُ ارْتَفَعَتْ.⁩ : ⁧نَعَمْ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ Laylā: Yes: books are new, decisions are important, prices have gone up. !« ⁧الأَسْعَارُ ارْتَفَعُوا⁩ » ⁧إِذَنْ عِنْدِي مُشْكِلَةٌ مَعَ عُنْوَانِ مَقَالِي لِلدَّرْسِ:⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luca: Then I have a problem with the title of my article for the course:        • The prices have gone up, with the male plural! ⁧صَحِّحْهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَرَاهُ سَلْمَى!⁩ ( ⁧تَضْحَكُ⁩ ) ⁧لَيْلَى:⁩ Laylā: (laughs) Correct it before you see it Salmā! What to notice. ⁧الجُمْلَةُ الفِعْلِيَّةُ⁩ The word "verbal" begins with the verb; and ⁧الجُمْلَةُ الاِسْمِيَّةُ⁩ The nominal sentence is the beginning of the word. ⁧يُطَابِقُهُ⁩ "Accords with him" (III, ⁧مُطَابَقَة⁩ The Commission shall adopt implementing acts in accordance with the procedure referred to in Article 21 (2). ⁧العَدَد⁩ The number of the certificate shall be indicated. ⁧الجِنْس⁩ The genus is the genus "Saint-God's." ⁧جَمْعُ غَيْرِ العَاقِلِ⁩ The plural of non-rational, i.e. of things and animals: the Arabic technical term. ⁧فَوْرًا⁩ "Shortly." ⁧ذَكِيّ⁩ Intelligent. ⁧مَقَال⁩ Article 1 is amended as follows: 2. Two types of phrase Minutes Nominal Phrase Translation ⁧رَفَعَتِ الحُكُومَةُ الأُجُورَ.⁩ ⁧الحُكُومَةُ رَفَعَتِ الأُجُورَ.⁩ The government has increased wages. Minutes Nominal Phrase Translation ⁧يَعْمَلُ الطُّلَّابُ فِي المَكْتَبَةِ.⁩ ⁧الطُّلَّابُ يَعْمَلُونَ فِي المَكْتَبَةِ.⁩ Students work in the library. — ⁧الطَّقْسُ جَمِيلٌ.⁩ The weather is good. The verbal sentence begins with the verb: verb + subject ( ⁧فَاعِل⁩ ) + complements. It is the normal order of narrative and chronicle. The nominal sentence begins with a name, the term "theme" ( ⁧مُبْتَدَأ⁩ ), followed by what is said about it, the "predicate" ( ⁧خَبَر⁩ ). The predicate may be an adjective, a name, a preposition with its complement, or a verbal sentence: ⁧الحُكُومَةُ رَفَعَتِ الأُجُورَ⁩ = theme ⁧الحُكُومَةُ⁩ + predicate ⁧رَفَعَتِ الأُجُورَ.⁩ What's the difference? The content is the same; It changes the focus. The nominal sentence highlights the subject (as far as the government is concerned, increased wages) or contrasts it with another. In the spoken language and dialects the SVO order is much more frequent than in the fuṣḥā written. 3. The agreement in the verbal sentence (verb first) Rule: the verb before the subject remains to the singular, but it accords in the genre. Subject Example Translation Single Male ⁧وَصَلَ الوَزِيرُ.⁩ The minister's here. male dual ⁧وَصَلَ الوَزِيرَانِ.⁩ The two ministers have arrived. male plural ⁧وَصَلَ الوُزَرَاءُ.⁩ The ministers have arrived. female singular ⁧وَصَلَتِ الوَزِيرَةُ.⁩ The Minister has arrived. female dual ⁧وَصَلَتِ الوَزِيرَتَانِ.⁩ The two minutes have arrived. female plural ⁧وَصَلَتِ الوَزِيرَاتُ.⁩ The minions have arrived. Two cases to be recognized. 1. If there are other words between the verb and the female subject, the verb may remain to the male: ⁧حَضَرَ الاِجْتِمَاعَ ثَلَاثُ مُوَظَّفَاتٍ⁩ Three staff members attended the meeting (but ⁧حَضَرَتْ⁩ is always correct). 2. With a plural over people, in the literary language the verb sometimes goes to female: ⁧قَالَتِ الأَعْرَابُ⁩ . In the newspapers you will almost always find the male: ⁧قَالَ الخُبَرَاءُ.⁩ The pronoun subject is inside the verb and does not repeat: ⁧وَصَلُوا⁩ They're here. When the subject has already been appointed, the verb takes the desinence of person: ⁧وَصَلَ الوُزَرَاءُ وَعَقَدُوا اجْتِمَاعًا⁩ The Ministers arrived and held a meeting. 4. The agreement in the nominal sentence (verb after) Rule: the verb after the subject agrees in everything: gender and number. Subject Example Translation male plural ⁧الوُزَرَاءُ وَصَلُوا.⁩ The ministers have arrived. female plural ⁧الوَزِيرَاتُ وَصَلْنَ.⁩ The minions have arrived. Subject Example Translation dual ⁧الوَزِيرَتَانِ وَصَلَتَا.⁩ · ⁧الوَزِيرَانِ وَصَلَا.⁩ The two ministers/the two minions have arrived. The same applies to the preaching adjectives: ⁧الطُّلَّابُ مُتْعَبُونَ⁩ , ⁧الطَّالِبَاتُ مُتْعَبَاتٌ.⁩ 5. The pluralities of things and animals Rule: a non-human plural ( ⁧جَمْعُ غَيْرِ العَاقِلِ⁩ ) is a singular female, in any position: verb, adjective, pronoun, demonstrative. Item Example Translation verb before ⁧اِرْتَفَعَتِ الأَسْعَارُ.⁩ Prices have gone up. verb after ⁧الأَسْعَارُ ارْتَفَعَتْ.⁩ Prices have gone up. adjective ⁧قَرَارَاتٌ مُهِمَّةٌ⁩ Important decisions pronoun ⁧قَرَأْتُ الكُتُبَ وَأَعَدْتُهَا.⁩ I read the books and returned them. demonstration ⁧هٰذِهِ المَشَارِيعُ⁩ these projects concerning ⁧المُدُنُ الَّتِي زُرْتُهَا⁩ the cities I visited Attention to its and the demonstration. ⁧هٰذِهِ⁩ (not ⁧هٰؤُلَاءِ⁩ ) e ⁧الَّتِي⁩ (not ⁧الَّذِينَ⁩ ) with the pluralities of things. ⁧هٰؤُلَاءِ⁩ and ⁧الَّذِينَ⁩ It's just for people. An exception to recognize. With few counted objects (3–10) sometimes you find the female plural: ⁧أَيَّامٌ مَعْدُودَاتٌ⁩ A few days is a classic style. In the modern language he always uses the singular female. 6. The tutor reads ten nominal titles; you transform each one into the first sentence of an article, with the verb to the perfect and a complement of time. 2. Correction. The tutor reads ten sentences with chord errors (some are correct): of which they are wrong and Correct them by word. 3. The theme in relief. Tell in two minutes what you did this week, putting at least three times in a feature with the pronoun for recovery ( ⁧هٰذَا الفِيلْمُ شَاهَدْتُهُ⁩ …, ⁧صَدِيقِي، اِلْتَقَيْتُ بِهِ⁩ …). 19. Typical errors Error Correction ⁧جَاءَ الطُّلَّابُجَاءُوا الطُّلَّابُ⁩ : verb before subject, singular  ⁧الطَّالِبَاتُ ذَهَبْنَالطَّالِبَاتُ ذَهَبُوا⁩ ⁧الأَسْعَارُ ارْتَفَعَتْالأَسْعَارُ ارْتَفَعُوا⁩ : plural of things = female singular ⁧الأَسْعَارُ ارْتَفَعَتْالأَسْعَارُ ارْتَفَعُوا⁩  ⁧هٰذِهِ الكُتُبُهٰؤُلَاءِ الكُتُبُ⁩ … ⁧القَرَارَاتُ الَّذِينَ⁩ … ⁧القَرَارَاتُ الَّتِي⁩ ⁧رَجُلٌ فِي المَكْتَبِ⁩ (There's a man) ⁧فِي المَكْتَبِ رَجُلٌ⁩  : ⁧الحُكُومَة⁩ is female ⁧أَعْلَنَتِ الحُكُومَةُأَعْلَنَ الحُكُومَةُ⁩ Translate    □ arrived ministers □ The ministers have arrived: in English the verb always agrees 20. Active booster review Question Answer The ministers have arrived (verb before · verb after) ⁧الوُزَرَاءُ وَصَلُوا⁩ · ⁧وَصَلَ الوُزَرَاءُ⁩ The minutes have arrived (verb before · after) ⁧الوَزِيرَاتُ وَصَلْنَ⁩ · ⁧وَصَلَتِ الوَزِيرَاتُ⁩ Prices rose (two orders) ⁧الأَسْعَارُ ارْتَفَعَتْ⁩ · ⁧اِرْتَفَعَتِ الأَسْعَارُ⁩ These projects are the projects which... … ⁧المَشَارِيعُ الَّتِي⁩ · ⁧هٰذِهِ المَشَارِيعُ⁩ There's a man in the office. ⁧فِي المَكْتَبِ رَجُلٌ.⁩ A friend came to see me. ⁧زَارَنِي صَدِيقٌ.⁩ Agreement ⁧الحُكُومَة⁩ · ⁧الفَرِيق⁩ · ⁧النَّاس⁩ f. sing. · m. sing. · plural "Shipped" · "syndacate" · "protesta" ⁧اِحْتِجَاج⁩ · ⁧نِقَابَة⁩ · ⁧إِضْرَاب⁩ Unemployment rate ⁧نِسْبَةُ البِطَالَةِ⁩ Arabic term for "plural of things" ⁧جَمْعُ غَيْرِ العَاقِلِ⁩ 21. Unit verification Twenty points; Exceeding at least 16. A - Agreement (8 points). Put the right shape: 1. ⁧◌⁩ ( ⁧خَرَجَ⁩ ) ⁧الطُّلَّابُ⁩ . · 2. ⁧الطُّلَّابُ ◌⁩ ( ⁧خَرَجَ⁩ ). · 3. ⁧◌⁩ ( ⁧خَرَجَ⁩ ) ⁧الطَّالِبَاتُ⁩ . · 4. ⁧الطَّالِبَاتُ ◌⁩ ( ⁧خَرَجَ⁩ ). · 5. ⁧الشَّوَارِعُ ◌⁩ ( ⁧مُزْدَحِم⁩ ). · 6. ⁧◌⁩ ( ⁧أَعْلَنَ⁩ ) ⁧الشُّرْطَةُ⁩ … · 7. ⁧الوَزِيرَانِ ◌⁩ ( ⁧وَصَلَ⁩ ). · 8. ⁧◌⁩ ( ⁧هٰذَا⁩ ) ⁧القَرَارَاتُ⁩ B · Order (6 points). Translate: 9. I have a question. · 10. There's a bar in front of the station. · 11. The bar is in front of the station. · 12. The manager informed us. · 13. Title: "The government lowers taxes" · 14. The first sentence of the article in the same title, with C - Vocabulary and translation (6 points). Translate into English: 15. ⁧أَعْلَنَتِ النِّقَابَةُ إِضْرَابًا.⁩ · 16. ⁧اِحْتَجَّ السُّكَّانُ عَلَى القَرَارِ.⁩ · 17. ⁧صَوَّتَتِ الأَغْلَبِيَّةُ لِصَالِحِ القَانُونِ.⁩ · 18. ⁧نِسْبَةُ البِطَالَةِ⁩ · 19. ⁧مِنْ حَقِّكَ أَنْ تَرْفُضَ.⁩ · 20. ⁧أَصْدَرَتِ الوِزَارَةُ بَيَانًا.⁩ 22. To switch to the next unit Steps to B1-09 if you have at least 16/20 and if in the Exercise 4 You have corrected all agreements with pluralities of things. In B1-09 studies on ḥāl, the complement describing the status of the subject or object as the action takes place ( ⁧وَصَلَ مُتْعَبًا⁩ He arrived tired.

title: The ḥāl: state during action
text: Lesson overview He arrived tired, he went out crying, they went in laughing, he left without saying anything, he uses adjectives, Gerundi and phrases with Arabic has only one construction for all these cases, the ḥāl ( ⁧الحَال⁩ , "the state"): a word to the indeterminate accusative ( ⁧وَصَلَ مُتْعَبًا⁩ ) or a sentence introduced by ⁧وَ⁩ ( ⁧خَرَجَتْ وَهِيَ تَبْكِي⁩ ). It is very common in stories, accounts and the chronicle, and its endings in -an are the key to figuring out who does what. Two weeks. Item Details Code B1-09 Level B1 · Module B1.2 ... Prerequisites B1-03 (participants), B1-08 Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 113–114), plus the EGY track Materials This unit, Grammar G49, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognize and use the ḥāl of a word, to the indeterminate accusative, granted with his • bearer ( ⁧صَاحِبُ الحَالِ⁩ ); 2. distinguish the ḥāl from the adjective ( ⁧رَأَيْتُ الرَّجُلَ مُسْرِعًا⁩ / ⁧الرَّجُلَ المُسْرِعَ⁩ ); 3. build the state phrase with ⁧وَ⁩ + pronoun, with direct imperfection and with ⁧وَقَدْ⁩ + perfect; 4. to express "without" with ⁧دُونَ أَنْ⁩ , ⁧بِدُونِ⁩ , ⁧بِلَا⁩ ; 5. use the most frequent adverbs ( ⁧مَعًا⁩ , ⁧جَمِيعًا⁩ , ⁧وَحْدَهُ⁩ , ⁧شَخْصِيًّا⁩ , ⁧مُبَاشَرَةً⁩ ); 6. translating the ḥāl in English with the adjective, the gerund, the while, the word "con', the word "con', the word "without'. Two-week plan. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 2: what is the ḥāl 2 Section 3: ḥāl of a word · exercise 1 · lexicon (first half) 3 Section 4: ḥāl or adjective? · year 2 4 Dialogue 2 · section 6: the state phrase · exercise 3 5 Section 6 (continued) · Exercise 4 6 Session with the tutor (oral production) 1) 7 Review · Read 1, first half 8 Section 7: + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + 5 · lexicon (second half) 9 Section 8: mode adverbs · exercise 6 10 Reading 1 complete · exercise 9 · Exercise 7–8 11 Translation (year 10) · Script B 12 Writing (year 11) · Script C 13 Oral production 2–3 14 Unit verification · active recall review 1. Dialogue 1 · The Feast of Karīm Maria could not go to the party for the new house of Karīm (B1-07) and asks Luke how it went. Arabic Translation ⁧مَارِيَا: كَيْفَ كَانَتْ حَفْلَةُ كَرِيم؟ آسِفَةٌ، لَمْ أَسْتَطِعْ أَنْ آتِيَ.⁩ Maria: How was the feast of Karīm? I'm sorry, I couldn't come. ⁧لُوكَا: كَانَتْ رَائِعَةً! وَصَلْتُ مُبَكِّرًا، فَوَجَدْتُ كَرِيم وَحْدَهُ فِي المَطْبَخِ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِلُ أَنْ يَطْبُخَ شَيْئًا.⁩ Luca: It was wonderful! I arrived early and found Karīm alone in the kitchen trying to cook something. ⁧مَارِيَا: كَرِيم يَطْبُخُ؟!⁩ Maria: Karīm What kitchen?! ⁧لُوكَا: نَعَمْ! وَكَانَ خَائِفًا جِدًّا مِنَ النَّتِيجَةِ. ثُمَّ جَاءَتْ إِيلِينَا تَحْمِلُ كَعْكَةً كَبِيرَةً، وَدَخَلَ بَاوْلُو ضَاحِكًا، لِأَنَّهُ صَعِدَ الطَّوَابِقَ الخَمْسَةَ سَيْرًا عَلَى الأَقْدَامِ.⁩ Yes! And he was very afraid of the result. Then came Elena with a big cake, and entered Paul laughing, because she had climbed the five floors on foot. ⁧مَارِيَا: وَالمِصْعَدُ؟⁩ What about the elevator? ⁧لُوكَا: مَا زَالَ مُعَطَّلًا! جَلَسْنَا جَمِيعًا عَلَى الشُّرْفَةِ نَأْكُلُ وَنَتَحَدَّثُ. وَفِي آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ خَرَجْنَا مَعًا وَنَحْنُ نُغَنِّي أَغَانِيَ عَرَبِيَّةً قَدِيمَةً.⁩ Again, it's broken! We all sat on the balcony eating and chatting. And at the end of the night, we went out singing old Arab songs together. ⁧مَارِيَا: تُغَنُّونَ؟! وَمَاذَا قَالَ الجِيرَانُ؟⁩ Did you sing?! And what did the neighbors say? ⁧نَزَلْنَا الدَّرَجَ بِسُرْعَةٍ دُونَ أَنْ نَنْظُرَ خَلْفَنَا!⁩ … ⁧لَا أَعْرِفُ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Luca: I don't know... we went down the stairs in a hurry without looking back! ⁧أَنْتُمْ مَجَانِينُ!⁩ ( ⁧تَضْحَكُ⁩ ) ⁧مَارِيَا:⁩ You're crazy! What to notice. Ḥāl of a word: ⁧مُبَكِّرًا⁩ (here adverb), ⁧وَحْدَهُ⁩ • alone • • alone • ⁧خَائِفًا⁩ (predicted by ⁧كَانَ⁩ , ḥāl!), ⁧ضَاحِكًا⁩ "Laughter' means: ⁧سَيْرًا عَلَى الأَقْدَامِ⁩ "Hiking' means: ⁧جَمِيعًا⁩ "All" is "all," ⁧مَعًا⁩ "Together" is the same. State Phrases: ⁧وَهُوَ يُحَاوِلُ⁩ • while looking for • • • • • • • • • • ⁧وَنَحْنُ نُغَنِّي⁩ "Singing" is a song. Direct imperfection after a verb of motion or position: ⁧جَاءَتْ⁩ … ⁧تَحْمِلُ⁩ She came in with the car. ⁧جَلَسْنَا⁩ … ⁧نَأْكُلُ⁩ We sat down and ate. ⁧دُونَ أَنْ نَنْظُرَ⁩ • without looking • • ⁧كَعْكَة⁩ Cake. ⁧أَغَانِيَ⁩ "Songs" (pl. of ⁧أُغْنِيَة⁩ , diptototo). ⁧مَجَانِينُ⁩ Crazy (pl. of ⁧مَجْنُون⁩ ). 2. What is the ḥāl The ḥāl responds to the question ⁧كَيْفَ؟⁩ How? in what state? and describes the subject or object at the time when the action takes place . Phrase Question Ḥāl Carrier ( ⁧صَاحِبُ الحَالِ⁩ ) ⁧وَصَلَ الوَفْدُ مُتَأَخِّرًا.⁩ How did the delegation arrive? ⁧الوَفْدُمُتَأَخِّرًا⁩ (subject) ⁧رَأَيْتُهَا جَالِسَةً فِي المَقْهَى.⁩ How did you see it? ⁧ـهَاجَالِسَةً⁩ (object) ⁧خَرَجَ وَهُوَ يَبْكِي.⁩ How did he get out? ⁧وَهُوَ يَبْكِي⁩ the subject ⁧خَرَجَ⁩ The ḥāl is an extra element: if you remove it, the sentence remains complete ( ⁧وَصَلَ الوَفْدُ⁩ ). This distinguishes him from the predicate of ⁧كَانَ⁩ and similar verbs ( ⁧كَانَ خَائِفًا⁩ "He was frightened" where the accusative is mandatory. 3. The ḥāl of a word Form: Indeterminate accusative . Agreement: gender and bearer number. The ḥāl is almost always a participle or an adjective. Carrier Example Translation Single Male ⁧عَادَ الطَّالِبُ سَعِيدًا.⁩ The student came back happy. female singular ⁧عَادَتِ الطَّالِبَةُ سَعِيدَةً.⁩ The student came back happy. male dual ⁧عَادَ الطَّالِبَانِ سَعِيدَيْنِ.⁩ The two students came back happy. male plural ⁧عَادَ الطُّلَّابُ سُعَدَاءَ.⁩ The students came back happy. female plural ⁧عَادَتِ الطَّالِبَاتُ سَعِيدَاتٍ.⁩ The students are happy again. object ⁧وَجَدْتُ البَابَ مَفْتُوحًا.⁩ I found the door open. The healthy male plural takes ⁧ـِينَ⁩ : ⁧دَخَلُوا ضَاحِكِينَ⁩ They came in laughing. The healthy female plural takes ⁧ـَاتٍ⁩ (with kasra, not the fatha). The diptotes as ⁧سُعَدَاءُ⁩ They only take one fatha: ⁧سُعَدَاءَ⁩ . Position. Usually after the verb and subject; may also be immediately after the verb, before the subject: ⁧وَصَلَ مُتَأَخِّرًا الوَفْدُ⁩ (journalistic style). 4. Ḥāl or adjective? The same participle may be ḥāl or adjective: the determination decides it. Example Function Translation ⁧رَأَيْتُ الرَّجُلَ مُسْرِعًا.⁩ ḥāl (undetermined after a given name) I saw the man running/running. ⁧رَأَيْتُ الرَّجُلَ المُسْرِعَ.⁩ adjective (determined as the name) I saw the hasty man. ⁧رَأَيْتُ رَجُلًا مُسْرِعًا.⁩ adjective (undefined name) I saw a hasty man. The rule of thumb. An indeterminate accusatory following a given name and responding to "how?" is a ḥāl. With an indefinite name the same form is usually an adjective. 5. Dialogue 2 · The award evening Laylā tells Luca about the final evening of the Beirut festival. Arabic Translation ⁧لُوكَا: لَيْلَى! شَاهَدْتُ حَفْلَ الخِتَامِ عَلَى الإِنْتَرْنِت. هَلْ فَازَ الفِيلْمُ المِصْرِيُّ؟⁩ Luca: Laylā! I saw the internet closing night. Did the Egyptian movie win? ⁧لَيْلَى: فَازَ بِالجَائِزَةِ الأُولَى! صَعِدَتِ المُخْرِجَةُ إِلَى المِنَصَّةِ وَهِيَ تَبْكِي مِنَ الفَرَحِ.⁩ Laylā: He won the first prize! The director went on stage crying with joy. ⁧رَأَيْتُهَا! وَوَقَفَ الجُمْهُورُ مُصَفِّقًا دَقَائِقَ طَوِيلَةً.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ I saw her! And the audience stood and applauded for long minutes. Arabic Translation ⁧لَيْلَى: وَأَنَا كُنْتُ جَالِسَةً فِي الصَّفِّ الأَوَّلِ أَكْتُبُ بِسُرْعَةٍ. ثُمَّ تَكَلَّمَتِ المُخْرِجَةُ هَادِئَةً، وَشَكَرَتْ فَرِيقَهَا وَاحِدًا وَاحِدًا.⁩ Laylā: And I was sitting in the front row writing fast. Then the director spoke calmly and thanked her team one by one. ⁧لُوكَا: وَهَلْ قَابَلْتِهَا شَخْصِيًّا؟⁩ And you met her in person? ⁧لَيْلَى: نَعَمْ، بَعْدَ الحَفْلِ. جَاءَتْ إِلَيَّ مُبْتَسِمَةً وَقَالَتْ إِنَّهَا تَعْرِفُ تَقَارِيرِي! خَرَجْتُ مِنَ القَاعَةِ وَأَنَا لَا أُصَدِّقُ.⁩ Laylā: Yes, after the evening. She came to me smiling and told me she knows my services! I walked out of the room and couldn't believe it. ⁧لُوكَا: وَغَدًا؟⁩ What about tomorrow? ⁧وَلٰكِنْ سَعِيدَةً!⁩ … ⁧غَدًا أَعُودُ إِلَى بَيْرُوت مُتْعَبَةً⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ Laylā: Tomorrow I return to Beirut tired... but happy! What to notice. ⁧وَهِيَ تَبْكِي⁩ "Crying" (state phrase with the pronoun). ⁧مُصَفِّقًا⁩ Claping (participle of form II as ḥāl). ⁧جَالِسَةً⁩ is preached by ⁧كُنْتُ⁩ ; ⁧أَكْتُبُ⁩ is an imperfect with value of ḥāl. ⁧هَادِئَةً⁩ • calmly (Lett. "calma": Italian often prefers a fashion complement. ⁧شَخْصِيًّا⁩ In person: ... ⁧مُبْتَسِمَةً⁩ Smiling, smiling. ⁧وَأَنَا لَا أُصَدِّقُ⁩ • without believing it (Lett. I don't think so. ⁧مُتْعَبَةً⁩ … ⁧سَعِيدَةً⁩ : two ḥāl Coordinate. ⁧حَفْلُ الخِتَامِ⁩ The closing evening is closed. ⁧الفَرَح⁩ "Joy" is the word. ⁧وَاحِدًا وَاحِدًا⁩ One by one. 6. The state phrase The ḥāl can be an entire sentence ( ⁧الجُمْلَةُ الحَالِيَّةُ⁩ ). Three buildings: Construction Example Translation ⁧وَ⁩ + pronoun + predicate ⁧دَخَلَ وَفِي⁩ · ⁧خَرَجَتْ وَهِيَ تَبْكِي.⁩ ⁧يَدِهِ كِتَابٌ.⁩ She came out crying. · He entered with a book in his hand. imperfect without ⁧وَ⁩ (after verbs of motion and position) ⁧جَلَسُوا يَنْتَظِرُونَ.⁩ · ⁧جَاءَ يَرْكُضُ.⁩ He came running. · They sat and waited. ⁧وَقَدْ⁩ + perfect (action already accomplished) ⁧عَادَ إِلَى قَرْيَتِهِ وَقَدْ تَغَيَّرَ كُلُّ⁩ He went back to his village, where everything had changed. ⁧شَيْءٍ.⁩ The ⁧و⁩ State ⁧وَاوُ الحَالِ⁩ ) does not mean "and": introduces the circumstance. It translates with ... ..while, with the gerund, with ... or with a relative, never with ... and... The pronoun refers to the bearer of ḥāl: ⁧خَرَجَ وَهُوَ⁩ …, ⁧خَرَجَتْ وَهِيَ⁩ …, ⁧خَرَجُوا وَهُمْ⁩ …. With the first person: ⁧خَرَجْتُ وَأَنَا⁩ …, ⁧خَرَجْنَا وَنَحْنُ⁩ …. ⁧وَقَدْ⁩ + perfect indicates a situation already achieved at the time of the main action: ⁧وَصَلْنَا وَقَدْ بَدَأَ الفِيلْمُ⁩ When we arrived, the film had already begun. 7. Without it Construction Example Translation ⁧دُونَ أَنْ⁩ / ⁧مِنْ دُونِ أَنْ⁩ + ⁧خَرَجَ دُونَ أَنْ يَقُولَ شَيْئًا.⁩ He came out without saying anything. conjunctive Construction Example Translation ⁧بِدُونِ⁩ / ⁧دُونَ⁩ + name or maṣdar ⁧دَخَلَ دُونَ⁩ · ⁧سَافَرَ بِدُونِ جَوَازِ سَفَرٍ.⁩ ⁧اسْتِئْذَانٍ.⁩ He left without a passport. · He entered without asking permission. ⁧بِلَا⁩ + name indefinite ⁧قَهْوَةٌ بِلَا سُكَّرٍ⁩ Coffee without sugar ⁧وَ⁩ + pronoun + denial ⁧خَرَجَ وَهُوَ لَا يَعْرِفُ الطَّرِيقَ.⁩ He went out without knowing the way. 8. Fashion adverbs Many expressions of fashion in -an are, grammatically, of ḥāl or similar constructions. In pausing reading the last word of the sentence is read with -ā (wa-ṣala mutaʾaḫḫirā), but within the sentence pronunciation -an. title: The tamyīz and the absolute complement
text: Lesson overview Two charges still, both very frequent in the language of information. The tamyīz ( ⁧التَّمْيِيز⁩ , "Specification" is precise with respect to what a quantity or comparison is worth: ⁧عِشْرُونَ كِتَابًا⁩ , ⁧أَكْثَرُ أَهَمِّيَّةً⁩ More importantly, ⁧اِزْدَادَ الوَضْعُ سُوءًا⁩ The situation has deteriorated. Thanks to tamyīz You can compare any adjective, even those that have no form. ⁧أَفْعَل⁩ . The absolute complement ( ⁧المَفْعُولُ المُطْلَقُ⁩ ) repeats maṣdar of the verb to say how or how much the action took place: ⁧اِرْتَفَعَتِ الأَسْعَارُ ارْتِفَاعًا كَبِيرًا⁩ The prices have increased significantly, ⁧شَكَرْتُهُ شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا⁩ . Two weeks. Item Details Code B1-10 Level B1 · Module B1.2 ... Prerequisites B1-04 (maṣdar), B1-09 Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 115–116), plus the EGY track Materials This unit, Grammar G50, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. use the tamyīz after the numbers from 11 a 99 and after ⁧كَمْ⁩ question; 2. make the comparative and superlative of each adjective with ⁧أَكْثَرُ⁩ / ⁧أَقَلُّ⁩ / ⁧أَشَدُّ⁩ + tamyīz; 3. use the tamyīz with the verbs of increase and decrease ( ⁧اِزْدَادَ⁩ , ⁧تَضَاعَفَ⁩ ) and measures; 4. recognize and use the absolute complement with an adjective, iḍāfa and to indicate the number of times; 5. recognise absolute complements ⁧شُكْرًا⁩ , ⁧طَبْعًا⁩ , ⁧جِدًّا⁩ , ⁧أَيْضًا⁩ ); 6. translating tamyīz and absolute complement with natural Italian adverbs and complements. Two-week plan. Dialogue 1 · What flight? Luca and Hudā compare flights to Cairo in July. Arabic Translation ⁧هُدَى: كَمْ رِحْلَةً وَجَدْتَ؟⁩ Hudā: How many flights have you found? ⁧لُوكَا: ثَلَاثَ رِحْلَاتٍ. الأُولَى مُبَاشِرَةٌ، وَالثَّانِيَةُ وَالثَّالِثَةُ عَبْرَ إِسْطَنْبُولَ وَأَثِينَا.⁩ Three flights. The first is directed, the second and third via Istanbul and Athens. ⁧هُدَى: المُبَاشِرَةُ أَقْصَرُ مُدَّةً طَبْعًا. وَكَمْ سَاعَةً تَسْتَغْرِقُ؟⁩ Hudā: Direct is shorter, of course. What is the tamyīz The tamyīz is an indefinite name to the accusative that removes ambiguity to a previous word: a number, a measure, a comparison, a verb of increase. The absolute complement The absolute complement is the maṣdar of the same verb to the accusative. It strengthens itself (it really does, it does); with an adjective, aiḍāfa or a number says how or how many times. title: The hypothetical period:إِذَا‎, ‎إِنْ‎, ‎لَوْ‎
text: Lesson overview If you come soon, call me "If I had time," I would come, "If I had known," I would have told you: Italian distinguishes the types of hypotheses with the times and ways of the verb. The Arabic distinguishes them mainly with the conjunction: ⁧إِذَا⁩ for actual or probable assumptions, ⁧إِنْ⁩ for possible (more formal), ⁧لَوْ⁩ for the unreal ones. In all three, surprisingly, the verb of the condition is almost always to the perfect , even when it comes to the future. You will also learn the neighboring conjunctions ( ⁧إِلَّا إِذَا⁩ Unless otherwise specified, ⁧حَتَّى لَوْ⁩ "Although" ⁧لَوْلَا⁩ If it isn't for the sake of the word, ⁧كُلَّمَا⁩ (a) the rules of the ⁧فَـ⁩ which introduces the consequence. Two weeks. Item Details Code B1-11 Level B1 · Module B1.2 ... Prerequisites B1-08 Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 117–118), plus the EGY track Materials This unit, Grammar G51, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. build real assumptions with ⁧إِذَا⁩ + perfect and the consequence to the present, future or imperative; 2. use the ⁧فَـ⁩ before the consequence; 3. recognise ⁧إِنْ⁩ with the perfect and the juxtative (formal style and fixed formulas); 4. to build unreal hypotheses with ⁧لَوْ⁩ + perfect and ⁧لَـ⁩ + perfect, even negative ( ⁧لَوْ لَمْ⁩ … ⁧لَمَا⁩ …); 5. use ⁧لَوْلَا⁩ , ⁧إِلَّا إِذَا⁩ , ⁧حَتَّى لَوْ⁩ , ⁧وَإِلَّا⁩ , ⁧كُلَّمَا⁩ , ⁧مَهْمَا⁩ ; 6. translate every type of hypothesis with the correct Italian times and ways. Two-week plan. He said, "If you find a colleague who works for you, there's no problem." ⁧هُدَى: إِذَا أَرَدْتَ، أَعْمَلُ مَكَانَكَ فِي الأُسْبُوعِ الأَوَّلِ.⁩ Hudā: If you want, I work for you the first week. ⁧لُوكَا: حَقًّا؟ إِنْ فَعَلْتِ ذٰلِكَ فَسَأَكُونُ مُمْتَنًّا لَكِ طَوَالَ حَيَاتِي!⁩ Really? If you do, I'll be grateful for you all my life! ⁧هُدَى: لَا تُبَالِغْ! وَلٰكِنْ بِشَرْطٍ: إِذَا ذَهَبْتَ إِلَى خَانِ الخَلِيلِيِّ، فَاشْتَرِ لِي فَانُوسًا.⁩ Hudā: Don't exaggerate! But on one condition: if you go to Khan el-Khalili, buy me a lantern. ⁧لُوكَا: اِتَّفَقْنَا. وَإِذَا لَمْ أَجِدْ فَانُوسًا جَمِيلًا؟⁩ Okay. What if I don't find a beautiful lantern? ( ⁧تَضْحَكُ⁩ ) ⁧فَلَا تَرْجِعْ!⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ Hudā: Then don't come back! (laughs) ⁧لُوكَا: وَالأُسْبُوعَانِ الآخَرَانِ؟⁩ What about the other two weeks? ⁧هُدَى: اِسْأَلْ بَاوْلُو. لَوْ كُنْتُ مَكَانَكَ لَسَأَلْتُهُ اليَوْمَ، قَبْلَ أَنْ يُخَطِّطَ لِعُطْلَتِهِ هُوَ.⁩ Hudā: Ask Paul. If I were you, I'd ask him today before he plans his vacation. ⁧لُوكَا: مَعَكِ حَقٌّ. لَوْ عَرَفْتُ هٰذَا أَمْسِ لَسَأَلْتُهُ فِي الاِجْتِمَاعِ!⁩ You're right. title: The exception:إِلَّا‎, ‎غَيْر‎, ‎سِوَى‎
text: Lesson overview They all came except KarīmI don't speak Arabic, I only have ten euros, the museum is open every day except Mondays.The exception and restriction are everywhere in public notices, regulations, conversation. Arabic mainly uses ⁧إِلَّا⁩ , with rules of chance changing according to the phrase, and then ⁧غَيْر⁩ , ⁧سِوَى⁩ , ⁧مَا عَدَا⁩ and ⁧بِاسْتِثْنَاءِ⁩ . The most useful construction of all is ⁧لَا⁩ … ⁧إِلَّا⁩ , the most natural way of saying "solo" . A week. Item Details Code B1-12 Level B1 · Module B1.2 ... Prerequisites B1-08 Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 119), plus the EGY track Materials This unit, Grammar G52, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. use ⁧إِلَّا⁩ in a complete affirmative sentence, with the exception of the accusative; 2. use the restriction ⁧لَا⁩ / ⁧مَا⁩ / ⁧لَمْ⁩ / ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ … ⁧إِلَّا⁩ • only, only in the case required by the sentence; 3. use ⁧غَيْر⁩ and ⁧سِوَى⁩ with the genitive; 4. recognize and use ⁧مَا عَدَا⁩ and ⁧بِاسْتِثْنَاءِ⁩ in formal texts; 5. distinguish ⁧فَقَط⁩ , ⁧لَا⁩ … ⁧إِلَّا⁩ and ⁧إِنَّمَا⁩ ; 6. translate the exception and restriction with the most natural Italian forms. Arabic Translation ⁧كَرِيم: مَا هٰذَا؟ مَا زَالَ أَمَامَكَ ثَلَاثَةُ أَسَابِيعَ!⁩ Karīm: What is this? title: The numerals: cardinals, ordinals, dates
text: Lesson overview Arabic numerals are famous for their difficulty: the genre is opposite from 3 a 10, the singular or plural name changing by digit, cases. In newspapers, numbers are almost always written in figures, but those who read aloud a news bulletin, those who say a date or those who translate a document need to know how they say. In this unit you put together the whole system, from units to millions, order them, fractions, dates in the two calendars and hours. Two weeks. Item Details Code B1-13 Level B1 · Module B1.2 ... Prerequisites B1-10 (tamyīz) Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 120–121), plus the EGY track Materials This unit, Grammar G53, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. Numbers 1–10 with the name (inverse genre from 3 a 10, plural genitive); 2. use numbers 11–99 with the singular accusative name, including 11 and 12; 3. use hundreds, thousands and millions under the singular name of genitive; 4. Form and grant of orders ( ⁧الأَوَّل⁩ , ⁧الحَادِي عَشَرَ⁩ , ⁧الحَادِي وَالعِشْرُونَ⁩ ); 5. to say fractions and percentages, dates (gregorian calendar and Egira), centuries, decades and hours; 6. read out figures and give them in a chronicle text. Two-week plan. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 2: the general framework 2 Section 3: 1–10 · year 1 · lexicon (first half) 3 Section 4: 11–99 · year 2 4 Section 5: hundreds, thousands, millions · year 3 5 Dialogue 2 · section 6: the order books · exercise 4 6 Session with the tutor (oral production) 1) 7 Review · Read 1, first half 8 Section 7: fractions and percentages · year 5 · lexicon (second half) 9 Section 8: dates, centuries, hours · exercise 6 10 Reading 1 complete · exercise 9 · Exercise 7–8 11 Translation (year 10) · Script B 12 Writing (year 11) · Script C 13 Oral production 2–3 14 Unit verification · active recall review 1. Dialogue 1 · Registration to the institute Luca calls the Cairo Institute to complete his membership. Arabic Translation ⁧المُوَظَّفَة: مَعْهَدُ اللُّغَاتِ، صَبَاحَ الخَيْرِ.⁩ The clerk: Institute of Languages, good morning. ⁧لُوكَا: صَبَاحَ النُّورِ. اِسْمِي لُوكَا، سَجَّلْتُ فِي الدَّوْرَةِ الصَّيْفِيَّةِ، وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَأَكَّدَ مِنْ بَعْضِ التَّفَاصِيلِ.⁩ Good morning. My name is Luca, I signed up for the summer class and I'd like to check out some details. ⁧المُوَظَّفَة: تَفَضَّلْ. رَقْمُ التَّسْجِيلِ؟⁩ Please. The registration number? ⁧لُوكَا: أَرْبَعَةٌ وَسَبْعُونَ، اثْنَانِ وَتِسْعُونَ.⁩ Seventy-four, ninety-two. ⁧المُوَظَّفَة: نَعَمْ، وَجَدْتُهُ. تَبْدَأُ الدَّوْرَةُ يَوْمَ السَّادِسِ مِنْ يُولْيُو، وَتَسْتَمِرُّ أَرْبَعَةَ أَسَابِيعَ.⁩ The employee: Yes, I found him. The course begins on 6 July and lasts four weeks. ⁧لُوكَا: وَكَمْ سَاعَةً فِي الأُسْبُوعِ؟⁩ And how many hours a week? ⁧المُوَظَّفَة: عِشْرُونَ سَاعَةً: أَرْبَعُ سَاعَاتٍ يَوْمِيًّا، مِنَ الأَحَدِ إِلَى الخَمِيسِ. وَهُنَاكَ أَيْضًا ثَلَاثُ رِحْلَاتٍ ثَقَافِيَّةٍ.⁩ The employee: Twenty hours: four hours a day, from Sunday to Thursday. There are also three cultural trips. ⁧لُوكَا: مُمْتَازٌ. وَالرُّسُومُ؟⁩ Great. What about the fee? ⁧المُوَظَّفَة: سَبْعُمِئَةٍ وَخَمْسُونَ دُولَارًا، دَفَعْتَ مِنْهَا ثُلُثَهَا، أَيْ مِئَتَيْنِ وَخَمْسِينَ. يَبْقَى خَمْسُمِئَةِ دُولَارٍ تَدْفَعُهَا فِي اليَوْمِ الأَوَّلِ.⁩ The employee: $700, $50, of which you paid a third, that is, $250. Five hundred dollars left to pay on the first day. ⁧لُوكَا: وَفِي أَيِّ صَفٍّ أَنَا؟⁩ Luca: And in what class are they? ⁧المُوَظَّفَة: فِي المُسْتَوَى الرَّابِعِ، القَاعَةُ رَقْمُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ، فِي الطَّابِقِ الثَّالِثِ. وَعَدَدُ الطُّلَّابِ فِي الصَّفِّ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ طَالِبًا وَطَالِبَةً.⁩ The employee: On the fourth level, room number twelve, on the third floor. The students in the class are eleven, between boys and girls. ⁧لُوكَا: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا. إِلَى اللِّقَاءِ فِي السَّادِسِ مِنْ يُولْيُو!⁩ Thank you very much. Goodbye to the 6 July! What to notice. ⁧أَرْبَعَةَ أَسَابِيعَ⁩ 4 weeks (0 to 0): 3–10 with the plural genitive, the male number because ⁧أُسْبُوع⁩ It's male. ⁧أَرْبَعُ سَاعَاتٍ⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثُ رِحْلَاتٍ⁩ : number without ⁧ة⁩ because the name is female. ⁧عِشْرُونَ سَاعَةً⁩ , ⁧أَحَدَ عَشَرَ طَالِبًا⁩ : 11–99 with the singular accusative. ⁧سَبْعُمِئَةٍ وَخَمْسُونَ دُولَارًا⁩ : the last element (50) decides the form of the name. ⁧خَمْسُمِئَةِ دُولَارٍ⁩ : 100 and multiples with the singular genitive. ⁧السَّادِسِ مِنْ يُولْيُو⁩ , ⁧المُسْتَوَى الرَّابِعِ⁩ , ⁧الطَّابِقِ الثَّالِثِ⁩ , ⁧اليَوْمِ الأَوَّلِ⁩ : order them. ⁧ثُلُثَهَا⁩ A third of them. ⁧القَاعَةُ رَقْمُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ⁩ : after ⁧رَقْم⁩ The number goes to the genitive. ⁧التَّفَاصِيل⁩ The details are given. ⁧الرُّسُوم⁩ The fee, the taxes. ⁧أَيْ⁩ • i.e. 2. The overall picture Number Name form Number Agreement Example 1, 2 singular, dual (the number follows as adjective) same genre ⁧كِتَابَانِ اثْنَانِ⁩ · ⁧كِتَابٌ وَاحِدٌ⁩ 3–10 plural genitive reverse genre ⁧ثَلَاثُ سَيَّارَاتٍ⁩ · ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ⁩ Number Name form Number Agreement Example 11–99 singular accusative own rules (section 4) ⁧عِشْرُونَ⁩ · ⁧خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ كِتَابًا⁩ ⁧سَيَّارَةً⁩ 100, 1000, 10⁶ singular genitive Unchangeable in the genre ⁧أَلْفُ سَيَّارَةٍ⁩ · ⁧مِئَةُ كِتَابٍ⁩ In the composite numbers, the last element pronounced shall be decided: ⁧مِئَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا⁩ ( 20 → singular accusation), ⁧أَلْفٌ وَثَلَاثَةُ طُلَّابٍ⁩ ( 3 → plural genitive). 3. From 1 a 10 1 and 2 they go after the name, as adjectives, and usually just to insist: ⁧عِنْدِي سُؤَالٌ وَاحِدٌ⁩ I only have one question. The name is normally sufficient ( ⁧سُؤَالٌ⁩ ) or the dual ( ⁧سُؤَالَانِ⁩ ). 3–10: the reverse genre. The number takes the ⁧ة⁩ if the singular of the name is male, do not take it if it is female: Name (single) Genre Example Translation ⁧كِتَاب⁩ m. ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ⁩ three books ⁧يَوْم⁩ m. ⁧خَمْسَةُ أَيَّامٍ⁩ five days ⁧سَيَّارَة⁩ f. ⁧ثَلَاثُ سَيَّارَاتٍ⁩ three machines ⁧سَاعَة⁩ f. ⁧أَرْبَعُ سَاعَاتٍ⁩ four hours ⁧طَالِبَة⁩ f. ⁧سَبْعُ طَالِبَاتٍ⁩ seven students Attention: it counts the kind of singular, not plural. ⁧رِجَال⁩ Is it a plural that looks feminine? No: the singular ⁧رَجُل⁩ is male → ⁧خَمْسَةُ رِجَالٍ⁩ . ⁧سِجِلَّات⁩ has the shape in ⁧ـات⁩ but the singular ⁧سِجِلّ⁩ is male → ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ⁩ ⁧سِجِلَّاتٍ.⁩ The case of the number depends on its function in the sentence: ⁧وَصَلَ ثَلَاثَةُ طُلَّابٍ⁩ (subject), ⁧رَأَيْتُ ثَلَاثَةَ طُلَّابٍ⁩ (object), ⁧مَعَ ثَلَاثَةِ طُلَّابٍ⁩ (after preposition). ⁧ثَمَانٍ⁩ * 8" (feminine) behaves like defects: ⁧ثَمَانِي سَاعَاتٍ⁩ in iḍāfa. 4. From 11 a 99 11 and 12  With a male name with a female name 11  ⁧إِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ طَالِبَةًأَحَدَ عَشَرَ طَالِبًا⁩ 12 (nominative)  ⁧اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ طَالِبَةًاثْنَا عَشَرَ طَالِبًا⁩ 12 (a.c. · Jan.) ⁧اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ طَالِبَةًاثْنَيْ عَشَرَ طَالِبًا⁩ 13–19: Unity follows the reverse genre, ⁧عَشَر⁩ / ⁧عَشْرَة⁩ follows the name genre; Both sides are invariant with the fatha. Example Translation ⁧ثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ كِتَابًا⁩ thirteen books ⁧ثَلَاثَ عَشْرَةَ سَيَّارَةً⁩ 13 machines ⁧خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا⁩ 15 days 20–90: forms in ⁧ـُونَ⁩ / ⁧ـِينَ⁩ ( ⁧عِشْرُونَ⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثُونَ⁩ … ⁧تِسْعُونَ⁩ ), the same for male and female, who decline as healthy plurals: ⁧عِشْرُونَ⁩ (No.), ⁧عِشْرِينَ⁩ (Ac., Jan.). 21–99: First the unit, then the ten, joined by ⁧وَ⁩ ; the unit follows the rules of 1–10 (1 and 2 granted, 3–9 Inverse genre): ⁧وَاحِدٌ وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا⁩ , ⁧إِحْدَى وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبَةً⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثَةٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ يَوْمًا⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ سَنَةً⁩ . Both sides decline. 5. Hundreds, thousands, millions Number Form Example 100 ⁧مِئَة⁩ (also written ⁧مِائَة⁩ , always read mea) ⁧مِئَةُ طَالِبٍ⁩ 200 ⁧مِئَتَانِ⁩ / ⁧مِئَتَيْنِ⁩ ; in iḍāfa ⁧مِئَتَا⁩ / ⁧مِئَتَا طَالِبٍمِئَتَيْ⁩  300–900 … ⁧أَرْبَعُمِئَةٍ⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثُمِئَةٍ⁩ ⁧خَمْسُمِئَةِ يُورُو⁩ 1000  ⁧أَلْفُ سَنَةٍأَلْف⁩ 2000 ⁧أَلْفَانِ⁩ / ⁧أَلْفَيْنِ⁩ ; in iḍāfa ⁧أَلْفَا⁩ / ⁧أَلْفَا شَخْصٍأَلْفَيْ⁩  3000–10000 … ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ آلَافٍ⁩ ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ آلَافِ كِتَابٍعَشَرَةُ آلَافٍ⁩ 11 000 and beyond , ⁧أَحَدَ عَشَرَ أَلْفًا⁩ ⁧عِشْرُونَ أَلْفَ زَائِرٍمِئَةُ أَلْفٍ⁩ 10⁶ · 10⁹ ⁧مِلْيُون⁩ (pl. ⁧مَلَايِينُ⁩ ) · ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ مَلَايِينِ نَسَمَةٍمِلْيَار⁩  The order of the big numbers. In the modern language we read from the greatest to the smallest: ⁧١٩٨٧⁩ = ⁧أَلْفٌ وَتِسْعُمِئَةٍ وَسَبْعَةٌ وَثَمَانُونَ⁩ . The classical form, from the smallest to the largest ( ⁧سَبْعَةٌ وَثَمَانُونَ وَتِسْعُمِئَةٍ وَأَلْفٌ⁩ ), is found in formal and religious texts: recognize it. The name after a large number follows the last element: ⁧أَلْفٌ وَخَمْسُمِئَةِ طَالِبٍ⁩ ( 500 → genitive), ⁧أَلْفَانِ وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا⁩ ( 20 → accusative). Practical reading. Many speakers simplify the endings when reading the news aloud; You look for at least the right gender and the right form of the name. 6. Dialogue 2 · Family dates Hudā Show Luca the family photos on the phone. Arabic Translation ⁧اُنْظُرْ، هٰذَا آدَمُ. أَتَمَّ أَمْسِ شَهْرَهُ السَّابِعَ!⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ Hudā: Look, this is Ādam. Yesterday he turned seven months! Arabic Translation ⁧لُوكَا: مَا شَاءَ اللهُ! وُلِدَ فِي الصَّيْفِ، صَحِيحٌ؟⁩ Luca: That's nice! He was born in the summer, wasn't he? ⁧، كَمَا⁩ « ⁧جْوِيلِيَة⁩ » ⁧أَوْ⁩ … ⁧نَعَمْ، فِي الخَامِسِ وَالعِشْرِينَ مِنْ يُولْيُو⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧يَقُولُ أَبِي! وَهٰذِهِ جَدَّتِي: سَتَحْتَفِلُ بِعِيدِ مِيلَادِهَا الخَامِسِ وَالثَّمَانِينَ⁩ ⁧فِي الشَّهْرِ القَادِمِ.⁩ Hudā: Yes, on July 25 ... or "juwiliya" , as my father says! And this is my grandmother: next month she celebrates her 85th birthday. ⁧لُوكَا: خَمْسٌ وَثَمَانُونَ سَنَةً! وَأَيْنَ تَعِيشُ؟⁩ Eighty-five years! And where does he live? ⁧هُدَى: فِي صَفَاقِسَ، فِي تُونِسَ. أَبِي جَاءَ إِلَى إِيطَالِيَا وَحْدَهُ فِي أَوَاخِرِ الثَّمَانِينِيَّاتِ، سَنَةَ أَلْفٍ وَتِسْعِمِئَةٍ وَتِسْعٍ وَثَمَانِينَ، وَتَعَرَّفَ إِلَى أُمِّي بَعْدَ سَنَتَيْنِ.⁩ Hudā: In Sfax, Tunisia. title: The diptotes: names that do not take the tanwīn
text: Lesson overview Why is it said? ⁧مِنْ مِصْرَ⁩ and not ⁧مِنْ مِصْرٍ⁩ , ⁧فِي مَدَارِسَ كَثِيرَةٍ⁩ and not ⁧فِي مَدَارِسٍ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ أَحْمَدَ⁩ and not ⁧مَعَ أَحْمَدٍ⁩ ? Why ⁧مِصْر⁩ , ⁧مَدَارِس⁩ and ⁧أَحْمَد⁩ are diptotic ( ⁧المَمْنُوعُ مِنَ الصَّرْفِ⁩ , are prevented from complete declension ,): they do not take the tanwīn and the genitive have a. You meet them from the first unit; now learn to recognize them, so as to read out loud with the right desinences proper names, plural and adjectives. It's the last unit on the module. B1.2. A week. Item Details Code B1-14 Level B1 · Module B1.2 ... Prerequisites B1-08 … B1-13 Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 122), plus the EGY track Materials This unit, Grammar G54, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. decline a diptoto: -u to the name, -a to the accusative and genitive, without tanwīn; 2. recognizing the four great groups of diptotes: own names, adjectives, plural tratti, words in ⁧ـَاء⁩ ; 3. know when a diptoto returns to decline normally (with the article and in iḍāfa); 4. distinguish plural diptotes ( ⁧مَدَارِسُ⁩ , ⁧وُزَرَاءُ⁩ ) from normal ( ⁧كُتُبٌ⁩ , ⁧طُلَّابٌ⁩ ); 5. read texts with their own names, cities and countries with correct desinences. Plan of the week. How to decline a diptoto Case Normal name (triptoto) Diptoto name  ⁧مَدَارِسُكِتَابٌ⁩ Accusative  ⁧مَدَارِسَكِتَابًا⁩ genitive ⁧مَدَارِسَكِتَابٍ⁩ Two differences: nothing tanwīn , and genitive equals the accusative (-a). The adjective that follows the diptotum is normally declined, with its tanwīn: ⁧مَدَارِسَ كَثِيرَةٍ.⁩ 3. When the diptototo is declined normally A diptototo returns triptototo (with kasra al genitivo) in two cases: 1. with the article: ⁧فِي المَدَارِسِ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ الأَصْدِقَاءِ⁩ , ⁧فِي السَّيَّارَةِ الحَمْرَاءِ⁩ ; 2. as the first term of aiḍāfa: ⁧فِي مَدَارِسِ المَدِينَةِ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِي⁩ , ⁧فِي أَجْمَلِ مَدِينَةٍ.⁩ The tanwīn but never returns, because with the article and in iḍāfa on tanwīn He's not there anyway. 7. Dialogue 2 · The cities of Laylā Laylā Tell Luca about his business trips. Arabic Translation ⁧لُوكَا: أَيْنَ كُنْتِ هٰذَا الشَّهْرَ؟ لَمْ أَرَكِ عَلَى الشَّاشَةِ.⁩ Where were you this month? I didn't see you on TV. ⁧لَيْلَى: سَافَرْتُ كَثِيرًا! بَدَأْتُ بِعَمَّانَ، ثُمَّ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى دِمَشْقَ وَبَغْدَادَ.⁩ Laylā: I traveled a lot! I started with Amman, then I went to Damascus and Baghdad. ⁧لُوكَا: وَمَعَ مَنْ؟⁩ And with whom? ⁧لَيْلَى: مَعَ زُمَلَاءَ مِنَ القَنَاةِ: مُصَوِّرٍ وَمُهَنْدِسِ صَوْتٍ. صَوَّرْنَا تَقْرِيرًا عَنْ شُعَرَاءَ شَبَابٍ يَكْتُبُونَ عَنْ مُدُنِهِمْ.⁩ Laylā: With colleagues from the channel: a cameraman and a sound engineer. We did a service on young poets who write about their cities. ⁧لُوكَا: مَوْضُوعٌ جَمِيلٌ. وَأَيْنَ قَابَلْتُمُوهُمْ؟⁩ Luca: Nice theme. And where did you meet them? ⁧لَيْلَى: فِي مَقَاهٍ قَدِيمَةٍ وَشَوَارِعَ ضَيِّقَةٍ، وَفِي مَكْتَبَاتٍ صَغِيرَةٍ. فِي بَغْدَادَ زُرْنَا شَارِعَ المُتَنَبِّي، شَارِعَ الكُتُبِ.⁩ Laylā: In old cafes and narrow alleys, and in small libraries. In Baghdad we visited via al- Mutanabbī, the way of books. ⁧لُوكَا: سَمِعْتُ عَنْهُ! وَمَتَى يُعْرَضُ التَّقْرِيرُ؟⁩ Luca: I've heard of it! title: Names of places and entities
text: Lesson overview After the names in person (ONO-01) and their Latin spellings (ONO-02), the track of names passes to the names of places and bodies. Casablanca is ⁧الدَّارُ البَيْضَاءُ⁩ , Tangier is Tanger in French and ⁧طَنْجَة⁩ in Arabic, Damascus is also ⁧الشَّام⁩ ; the Arab Republic of Egypt is listed in the addresses as ⁧ج.م.ع⁩ ; UNESCO is ⁧اليُونِسْكُو⁩ but also the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization. In this unit you learn to recognize the place names in their variants, to break down the long names of the institutions, to dissolve acronyms and abbreviations and to read an Arabic address. They are reading and transcription skills, useful to anyone working with documents, news and public sources. Two weeks. Item Details Code ONO-03 Level B1 · Onomastic trace Prerequisites ONO-01, ONO-02, A2-09 (entities and offices); form B1.2 exceeded Estimated time 10–12 hours · two weeks (weeks 124–125), plus the EGY track Materials This unit, an atlas or an online map in Arabic, voice synthesis scripts, tutor session Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognizing the Arab names of countries, with and without article, in the short form and in the official form; 2. link Arabic toponyms to their Italian, French and English forms, and vice versa; 3. recognizing frequent geographical elements in place names ( ⁧بِئْر⁩ , ⁧عَيْن⁩ , ⁧وَادٍ⁩ , ⁧جَبَل⁩ , ⁧رَأْس⁩ , ⁧تَلّ⁩ …); 4. break down and translate long names of international ministries, bodies and organisations; 5. loosen the most common abbreviations ( ⁧ج.م.ع⁩ , ⁧ص.ب⁩ ., ⁧د⁩ ., ⁧م⁩ ., ⁧ق.م⁩ .); 6. read and write an Arabic address. Two-week plan. Dialogue 1 · Tanger, Tangier, Ṭanǧa At the police station. Karīm, the interpreter of Fès, helps Luca to read a list of Moroccan cities written French. Arabic Translation ⁧لُوكَا⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم، هٰذِهِ القَائِمَةُ مَكْتُوبَةٌ بِالفَرَنْسِيَّةِ:⁩ “Tanger, Oujda, Ksar el-Kébir”. ⁧كَيْفَ تُكْتَبُ بِالعَرَبِيَّةِ؟⁩ Luca: Karīm, this list is written in French: "Tanger, Oujda, Ksar el-Kébir" . How do they write in Arabic? ⁧كَرِيم:⁩ Tanger ⁧هِيَ طَنْجَة، بِالطَّاءِ. وَ⁩ Oujda ⁧هِيَ وَجْدَة: الـ⁩ • • • ⁧الفَرَنْسِيَّةُ وَاوٌ.⁩ Karīm: “Tanger” is Ṭanǧa, with ṭāʾ. E .Oujda is Waǧda: the French "ou" is a wāw. ⁧لُوكَا⁩ : ⁧وَ⁩ Ksar el-Kébir ⁧؟⁩ Luke: What about Ksar el-Kébir? ⁧كَرِيم⁩ : ⁧القَصْرُ الكَبِيرُ.⁩ Ksar ⁧هِيَ⁩ « ⁧قَصْر⁩ » ⁧، وَلٰكِنْ فِي المَغْرِبِ نَنْطِقُهَا بِلَا⁩ ⁧حَرَكَةٍ بَعْدَ القَافِ.⁩ Karīm: Al-Qaṣr al-Kabīr. Ksar isqaṣrIn Morocco we pronounce it without voice after the qāf. ⁧لُوكَا⁩ : ⁧فَهِمْتُ. وَ⁩ • Casablanca ⁧؟ لَيْسَتْ كَلِمَةً عَرَبِيَّةً!⁩ Got it. And "Casablanca"? It's not an Arabic word! ⁧وَبِالعَرَبِيَّةِ⁩ .« ⁧البَيْتُ الأَبْيَضُ⁩ » ⁧صَحِيحٌ، هِيَ إِسْبَانِيَّةٌ، وَمَعْنَاهَا⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧نَقُولُ: الدَّارُ البَيْضَاءُ. التَّرْجَمَةُ نَفْسُهَا!⁩ Karīm: Right, it's Spanish and it means white house. In Arabic we say ad-Dār al-Bayḍāʾ: the same thing translated! ⁧لُوكَا⁩ : ⁧وَمَدِينَتُكَ؟⁩ • Fès ⁧أَمْ⁩ • Fez ⁧؟⁩ What about your city? "Fès" or "Fez"? ⁧كَرِيم⁩ : ⁧كِلَاهُمَا! الفَرَنْسِيُّونَ يَكْتُبُونَ⁩ • Fès ⁧، وَالإِنْجِلِيزُ⁩ • Fez ⁧، وَنَحْنُ نَكْتُبُ⁩ ⁧فَاس. وَلَا تَنْسَ: فِي المَغْرِبِ تُكْتَبُ الأَسْمَاءُ فِي الوَثَائِقِ الرَّسْمِيَّةِ بِالعَرَبِيَّةِ⁩ ⁧وَبِالحُرُوفِ اللَّاتِينِيَّةِ مَعًا.⁩ Karīm: Both of you! title: The journalistic title
text: Lesson overview With the module B1.3 begin to read real or constructed texts as real, without vowels. The first meeting with an Arabic newspaper is the title: a few words, no verb or verb to the imperfect for a past fact, maṣdar in chain, two points and quotes. In this unit you learn the fixed structures of Arabic titles, the vocabulary used there ( ⁧إِثْرَ⁩ , ⁧وَسَطَ⁩ , ⁧عَقِبَ⁩ , ⁧حَصِيلَة⁩ , ⁧جَدَل⁩ ), to distinguish title, subtitle and attack of the article, and to translate a title into a natural Italian title. It is also the basis of the press review from open sources (INT track). Two weeks. Item Details Code B1-15 Level B1 · Module B1.3 Real Texts (M) Prerequisites Modules B1.1 and B1.2; ONO-03 Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 126–127), plus the EGY track Materials This unit, Grammar G55, dictionary by root, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor; optional: the home page of a news site in Arabic Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognize the six main types of Arabic title and their grammar; 2. to understand the present journalistic (imperfect for a past fact) and the chain of maṣdar; 3. read the titles with quote and source ( ⁧الوَزِيرُ⁩ Questions and negatives ( ⁧لَا زِيَادَةَ⁩ …); 4. use the prepositions typical of the titles: ⁧إِثْرَ⁩ , ⁧عَقِبَ⁩ , ⁧وَسَطَ⁩ , ⁧جَرَّاءَ⁩ , ⁧رَغْمَ⁩ , ⁧بَعْدَ⁩ ; 5. distinguish title, eyelet, subtitle and attack ( ⁧المُقَدِّمَة⁩ ); 6. translate an Arabic title with a natural Italian title and similar length. Two-week plan. The present journalistic In titles imperfection ( ⁧المُضَارِع⁩ ) usually indicates a fact that has already happened, as in English "The government announces" .
