title: The future with ḥa-: projects, invitations, appointments
text: Lesson overview With the present (EGY-03) and the past (EGY-04) tales; with the future organize. In Egyptian the future is very simple: ḥa- in front of the imperfect (ḥaktib (I shall write to the House) miš (miš ḥaktib). In this unit you use it to make projects, invite, accept and refuse with politeness, set an appointment: the situations that you will live every day in Cairo, and that prepare Luke's arrival in July. Six weeks, in parallel with B1-12, B1-13 and B1-14. Item Details Code EGY-05 Level B1 · EGY track (Egyptian Cairo) Prerequisites EGY-04 Estimated time 8–9 hours · six weeks (weeks 119–124), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a tutor or Egyptian conversation partner, tutor recordings on the phone Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. to form and deny the future with ḥa- and miš ḥa-; 2. expressing intentions (nāwi) and plans; 3. invite, accept and refuse in a courteous manner; 4. set a place, day and time for an appointment, and move it; 5. use future expressions of time (bukra, baʿd bukra, il-usbūʿ ig-gayy, kamān šuwayya). Six-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). Week Block 1 Block 2 119 Dialogue 1 with transliteration · section 2 Section 3: Conjugation and denial · exercise 1 120 Section 4: the future time · exercise 2 Vocabulary · exercise 3 121 Section 5: invite, accept, reject · exercise 4 Section 6: appointments · exercise 5 122 Dialogue 2 · section 7: intentions Exercise 6 · Script B 123 Oral production 1–2 with the tutor Review · exercise 7 124 Oral production 3 Unit verification 1. Dialogue 1 · Dinner for Mīna Šarīf Call Luke to invite him to a dinner: Mīna He goes to Egypt for the summer. Egyptian Transliteration Translation ⁧شريف: ألو، لوكا؟ إنت فاضي يوم الجمعة بالليل؟⁩ Šarīf: alō, Lūka? inta fāḍi yōm ig-gumʿa bi-l-lēl? ŠarīfHello, Luca? Are you free Friday night? ⁧لوكا: الجمعة؟ أظن آه. ليه؟⁩ Lūka: ig-gumʿa? aẓunn āh. lēh? Friday? I think so. Why? Šarīf: ḥaniʿmil ʿaša li-Mīna ʾabl but Šarīf: Let's have dinner for Mīna ⁧هنعمل عشا لمينا قبل ما يسافر⁩ : ⁧شريف⁩ yisāfir Maṣr. ḥayuʾʿud hināk šahrēn. before he leaves for Egypt. He'll be there. ⁧مصر. هيقعد هناك شهرين.⁩ Two months. Egyptian Transliteration Translation ⁧لوكا: حلو أوي! فين؟⁩ Lūka: ḥilw ʾawi! fēn? Beautiful! Where? ⁧شريف: عندي في البيت. هطبخ ملوخية وفراخ.⁩ Šarīf: ʿandi fi l-bēt. ḥaṭbuḫ mulūḫiyya wi-frāḫ. Šarīf: At my house. I'll cook. mulūḫiyya And chicken. ⁧لوكا: إنت هتطبخ؟!⁩ Lūka: inta ḥatuṭbuḫ?! Luca: Will you cook?! … ⁧أيوه، وماما هتساعدني⁩ ( ⁧بيضحك⁩ ) ⁧شريف:⁩ ⁧على الفيديو!⁩ Šarīf: (biyiḍḥak) aywa, wi-māma ḥatsaʿidni… ʿa l-vidyo! Šarīf: (laughs) Yes, and Mom will help me... on video! ⁧لوكا: طب أجيب إيه معايا؟⁩ Lūka: ṭab, agīb ēh maʿāya? So what do I bring? ⁧شريف: ولا حاجة، إنت ضيف.⁩ Šarīf: wala ḥāga, inta ḍēf. Šarīf: Nothing, you're a guest. ⁧لوكا: لا، لازم أجيب حاجة. هجيب حلويات.⁩ Lūka: laʾ, lāzim agīb ḥāga. ḥagīb ḥalawiyyāt. No, I have to bring something. I'll bring some sweets. ⁧شريف: ماشي، زي ما تحب. الساعة تمانية، تمام؟⁩ Šarīf: māši, zayy ma tḥibb. is-sāʿa tamanya, tamām? Šarīf: All right, whatever. Eight o'clock, all right? ⁧لوكا: تمام. بس ممكن أتأخر شوية، علشان هخلص الشغل الساعة سبعة ونص.⁩ Lūka: tamām. bass mumkin atʾaḫḫar šuwayya, ʿalašān ḥaḫallaṣ iš-šuġl is- sāʿa sabʿa w-nuṣṣ. Okay. But I might be a little late, because I finish working at 7:30. Šarīf: wala yhimmak. mistanniyyīnak! Šarīf: Don't worry. You. ⁧ولا يهمك. مستنيينك!⁩ : ⁧شريف⁩ We wait! What to notice.ḥaniʿmil We're gonna do it. ḥayuʾʿud It shall be: ḥaṭbuḫ "Cucinerò" is the name of the novelist. ḥatsaʿidni "He'll help me," ḥagīb I'll carry it, ḥaḫallaṣ The future with ḥa-. fāḍi (fuṣḥā ⁧فَارِغ⁩ ). ʾabl but + imperfect ... before it is. agīb Port, port and port (verb) gāb). mulūḫiyya : green soup, Egyptian national dish; frāḫ • chickenfuṣḥā ⁧فِرَاخ⁩ ........................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................... ḍēf "Guest" is a guest. ḥalawiyyāt "Dolci" zayy ma tḥibb As you prefer, it is. mumkin + imperfect may be that, I could actually. mistanniyyīnak We are waiting for you (plural participle + suffix). 2. The Egyptian future and the fuṣḥā Fuṣḥā Egyptian Translation ⁧سَأَكْتُبُ⁩ ḥaktib I'll write ⁧سَيَذْهَبُ⁩ ḥayrūḥ will go ⁧لَنْ أُسَافِرَ⁩ miš ḥasāfir I won't leave. ḥa- or has-? Cairo feels like it. ḥa- is ha- (with light h), especially in the fast talk: haktib, hanrūḥ. They're the same thing; in this course we write ḥa-. Future and present. As in English, the present with b- can indicate a near and planned future: bukra barūḥ il-gamʿa I'm going to college tomorrow. ḥa- stresses the intention or prediction. 3. Conjugation and Denial The future is formed by ḥa- + simple imperfect (without b-). Person yiktib yirūḥ yākul ana ḥaktib ḥarūḥ ḥākul inta ḥatiktib ḥatrūḥ ḥatākul inti ḥatiktibi ḥatrūḥi ḥatākli huwwa ḥayiktib ḥayrūḥ ḥayākul hiyya ḥatiktib ḥatrūḥ ḥatākul iḥna ḥaniktib ḥanrūḥ ḥanākul intu ḥatiktibu ḥatrūḥu ḥatāklu humma ḥayiktibu ḥayrūḥu ḥayāklu Denial Is Always miš : miš ḥaktib I won't write, miš ḥanrūḥ We're not going. Never but...-š with the future. With the pronouns: ḥaʾullak I'll tell you, ḥašufak Bukra ... I see you tomorrow... ḥakallimha I'll call her. 4. The Future Time English Egyptian tomorrow · the day after tomorrow bukra · baʿd bukra tomorrow morning · tomorrow night bukra ṣ-ṣubḥ · bukra bi-l-lēl next week · next month il-usbūʿ ig-gayy · iš-šahr ig-gayy next year is-sana g-gayya in one hour · between two days baʿd sāʿa · baʿd yomēn I'll be back soon. kamān šuwayya Right away. ʿala ṭūl · dilwaʾti before · after ʾabl but · baʿd but (+ imperfect or perfect) baʿd with the future shall be ḥawṣal baʿd sāʿa Arrival in an hour. Remember: min with the past is worth "fa" (EGY-04). 5. Invite, accept, reject Function Egyptian Translation invite tīgi maʿāna? · ēh raʾyak nitʿašša Sawa? · ana ʿāzmak ʿala ʾahwa Are you coming with us? · How about dinner together? · I offer you a coffee propose Yalla Bina! · but tīgi… Let's go! · Why don't you come... accept māši · tamām · bi-kull surūr · ʾakīd! All right · Perfect · With pleasure · Sure! refuse with grace maʿlišš, miš ḥaʾdar · ʿandi mišwār · marra tanya in šāʾ allāh I'm sorry, I can't · I have a commitment · Another time, if God wills thank you mutašakkir ʾawi · tislam Thank you very much · Thank you for the invitation to refuse in Egypt. A dry "no" is rude. Thanks, you give a reason (also vague: ʿandi mišwār I have a commission to do and it opens up to another occasion (marra tanya). Often a first refusal is part of the courtesy, and he who invites insists: lāzimYou must! ʿazam / ʿāzim Invite, offer... ʿāzmak I'll buy it. The inviter usually pays. 6. Setting up an appointment Function Egyptian Translation ask nitʾābil Imta? · nitʾābil fēn? When do I see you? · Where do we see each other? propose ēh raʾyak bukra is-sāʿa Sit? How about tomorrow at 6:00? confirm ittafaʾna · ʿala l-maʿād All right, I'll see you at the appointment. move mumkin nʾaggil li-baʿd Bukra? Can we reschedule until the day after tomorrow? warning a delay ḥatʾaḫḫar ʿašar daʾāyiʾ, maʿlišš I'm ten minutes late. maʿād • appointment (fuṣḥā ⁧مَوْعِد⁩ ). ʿala l-maʿād (a) punctual; the appointment is not possible. The Egyptian weather is more elastic than the Italian one, but for work appointments and trains punctuality counts. 7. Dialogue 2 · I'll wait for you at the airport After dinner, Šarīf and Luke talk about July. Egyptian Transliteration Translation ⁧شريف: إنت هتوصل القاهرة إمتى بالظبط؟⁩ Šarīf: inta ḥatiwṣal il-Qāhira imta bi-ẓ- ẓabṭ? Šarīf: When do you arrive in Cairo exactly? ⁧لوكا: يوم تلاتة يوليو، الساعة خمسة العصر.⁩ Lūka: yōm talāta yulyu, is-sāʿa ḫamsa l-ʿaṣr. Luca: July three, at 5 p.m. ⁧شريف: تحفة! أنا كمان هكون في مصر في يوليو. هستناك في المطار.⁩ Šarīf: tuḥfa! ana kamān ḥakūn fi Maṣr fi yulyu. ḥastannāk fi l-maṭār. Šarīf: Great! I'll be in Egypt in July too. I'll wait for you at the airport. ⁧لوكا: بجد؟ مش عايز أتعبك.⁩ Lūka: bi-gadd? miš ʿāyiz atʿibak. Really? title: The imperative, indications and transport
text: Lesson overview In Cairo you will spend a lot of time asking for the road, taking taxi, metro and microbus, and understanding directions given quickly:ḫušš yimīn, w-ba'dēn ʿala ṭūl…». In this unit learn the Egyptian imperative (iktib, rūḥ, ḫud, taʿāla) and its negation (ma-truḥš), the words of the directions and the phrases to move by means. Six weeks, in parallel with ONO-03, B1-15 and B1-16. Item Details Code EGY-06 Level B1 · EGY track (Egyptian Cairo) Prerequisites EGY-05 Estimated time 8–9 hours · six weeks (weeks 125–130), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a tutor or Egyptian conversation partner, a map of Cairo (also online) Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. to form the affirmative and negative imperative, to a man, to a woman, to several persons; 2. use the most frequent irregular imperatives (taʿāla, hāt, ḫud, kul); 3. ask for the road and understand directions (right, left, straight, traffic light, square); 4. take a taxi, the metro and the microbus: give the address, ask for the price, let you leave; 5. ask and give practical advice on travel. Six-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). title: The possession, the family and the house
text: Lesson overview In Egypt the family is the first topic of conversation: who are you, who are yours, where they live, how many children they have. In this unit you learn to say "My, your, your" in Egyptian, with the suffixes (bitna "our house," ʾōḍti My room is with the word bitāʿ , typical of dialect (il-mobāyl bitāʿi My cell phone (s); kinship names, with the distinction between ʿamm and ḫāl that the Italian does not do; The vocabulary of the house and the apartment. Six weeks, in parallel with B1-17, B1-18 and B1-19. Item Details Code EGY-07 Level B1 · EGY track (Egyptian Cairo) Prerequisites EGY-06 Estimated time 8–9 hours · six weeks (weeks 131–136), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a tutor or Egyptian conversation partner, some photos (also taken from the web) for oral production Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. use possessive suffixes with names, even those in -a (ʾōḍa → ʾōḍti) and with aḫḫ (abūya, aḫūya); 2. use bitāʿ, bitāʿit, bitūʿ and ask who it is?bitāʿ mīn?); 3. present a family with Egyptian kinship names; 4. describe a house or apartment: rooms, furniture, floor, rent; 5. distinguish ʿandi "ho" is the name of the manufacturer. maʿāya I have with me and bitāʿi It's mine. Six-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). Egyptian Transliteration Translation ⁧شريف: بص، دي صور بيتنا في شبرا. ماما بعتتهالي امبارح.⁩ Šarīf: buṣṣ, di ṣuwar bitna fi Šubra. māma baʿatithāli mbāriḥ. Šarīf: Look, these are the photos of our house in Shubra. Mom sent them to me yesterday. ⁧لوكا: حلوة أوي! دي الصالة؟⁩ Lūka: ḥilwa ʾawi! di ṣ-ṣāla? Beautiful! Is this the living room? Hāla, with their three children. ⁧؟⁩ « ⁧عمي⁩ » ⁧؟ مش⁩ « ⁧خالي⁩ » ⁧لوكا:⁩ Lūka: «ḫāli»? miš «ʿammi»? Luke:ḫāli»? Notʿammi»? ⁧شريف: لأ! العم أخو الأب، والخال أخو الأم. في العربي لازم تعرف الفرق!⁩ Šarīf: laʾ! il-ʿamm aḫu l-abb, wi-l-ḫāl aḫu l-umm. fi l-ʿarabi lāzim tiʿraf il-farʾ! Šarīf: No! The ʿamm is the father's brother, the ḫāl He's the mother's brother. In Arabic you must know the difference! ⁧لوكا: في الإيطالي هي نفس الكلمة! وولاد خالك، بتشوفهم كتير؟⁩ Lūka: fi l-iṭāli hiyya nafs il-kilma! wi- wlād ḫālak, bitšufhum kitīr? Luca: In Italian it's the same word! And your cousins, do you see them often? ⁧شريف: كل جمعة! بنتغدى كلنا عند تيتة. العيلة المصرية كبيرة، ولازم نتقابل.⁩ Šarīf: kull gumʿa! binitġadda kullina ʿand tēta. il-ʿēla l-maṣriyya kbīra, wi- lāzim nitʾābil. Šarīf: Every Friday! Let's all have lunch at Grandma's. The Egyptian family is big, and we need to meet. ⁧لوكا: وتيتة ساكنة فين؟⁩ Lūka: wi-tēta sakna fēn? And where does grandmother live? ⁧شريف: في نفس العمارة، في الدور التاني. وإحنا في الخامس.⁩ Šarīf: fi nafs il-ʿimāra, fi d-dōr it-tāni. w-iḥna fi l-ḫāmis. ŠarīfIn the same building, on the second floor. And we're on the fifth. ⁧لوكا: يعني لما الأسانسير يعطل، إنتو اللي بتنزلوا لتيتة!⁩ Lūka: yaʿni lamma l-asansēr yiʿaṭṭal, intu lli bitinzilu li-tēta! Luke: So when the elevator breaks down, you go down to your grandmother! Šarīf: bi-ẓ-ẓabṭ! wi-tēta bitʾūl: Šarīf: Exactly! And the grandmother says, "So." ⁧دي رياضة⁩ » ⁧بالظبط! وتيتة بتقول:⁩ : ⁧شريف⁩ riyāḍa līkumDo sports! « ⁧ليكم!⁩ What to notice. Possession with the suffixes: bitna is our home ʾōḍti My room is mamtak your mother, ḫāli "My uncle" mirātu His wife, wladhum, their children, with bitāʿ: il-balakōna btaʿitna Our balcony is located in the heart of the city. btāʿit mīn? "Who's"? ʾōḍit Yāsmīn The chamber of YāsmīnIn front of a complement the -a becomes -it (like the tāʾ marbūṭa in fuṣḥā). ṭanṭ "Zia" is an affectionate title for family ladies or family friends. tēta "Grandma" is a song by American singer-songwriter and singer-songwriter. kullina "all of us." baʿatithāli "Me sent them" (baʿat + en + ha + li). 2. The possession in Egyptian and in fuṣḥā Fuṣḥā Egyptian Translation ⁧بَيْتُنَا⁩ · ⁧بَيْتِي⁩ bēti · bitna my home · our house ⁧غُرْفَتِي⁩ ʾōḍti my room ⁧أَخِي⁩ · ⁧أَبِي⁩ abūya · aḫūya my father · my brother ⁧سَيَّارَتِي⁩ ʿarabiyyiti · il-ʿarabiyya btaʿti my car ⁧لِمَنْ هٰذَا؟⁩ from btāʿ mīn? Whose is this? ⁧عِنْدِي شَقَّةٌ⁩ ʿandi šaʾʾa I have an apartment As in fuṣḥā, possession is expressed by the suffixes on the name. Plus, the Egyptian has bitāʿ , a word that means "di," belonging to "di" and which is put after the name with the article. 3. The possessive suffixes Person bēt (home) ʾōḍa (room) abb (father) ana bēti ʾōḍti abūya inta bētak ʾōḍtak abūk inti bētik ʾōḍtik abūki huwwa bētu ʾōḍtu abūh hiyya bitha ʾoḍitha abūha iḥna bitna ʾoḍitna abūna intu bitkum ʾoḍitkum abūkum humma bithum ʾoḍithum abūhum Three rules. 1. The names in -a take -it- (or -t-) before the suffix: šaʾʾa → šaʾʾiti, šaʾʾitak; ʿarabiyya → ʿarabiyyiti; ʾōḍa → ʾōḍti, ʾoḍitha. 2. The long vowel shortens before two consonants: bēt + na → bitna, ʾōḍit + ha→ ʾoḍitha. In front of a suffix beginning with vowel remains long: bētak, bētu. 3. abb and aḫḫ have special shapes with -ū-: abūya, abūk, abūh; aḫūya, aḫūk, aḫūha. Without suffix, in front of a name: abu Šarīf, aḫu māma. 4. bitāʿ Forms. bitāʿ agree with the possession, not the owner.  Masculine Feminine Plural base form bitāʿ bitāʿit bitūʿ + ana bitāʿi bitaʿti bitūʿi + inta bitāʿak bitaʿtak bitūʿak  Masculine Feminine Plural + hiyya bitaʿha bitaʿitha bituʿha + iḥna bitaʿna bitaʿitna bituʿna Examples: il-mobāyl bitāʿi My cell phone is in the middle of it. iš-šanṭa btaʿti My purse is actually okub bitūʿi My books. After a word that ends in vowel the initial i falls: il-ʿarabiyya btaʿtak. When to use bitāʿ. 1. With foreign words and long words, where the suffix sounds strange: the-laptop bitāʿi, il-asansēr bitāʿ on- ʿimāra. 2. To highlight or contrast: from miš bitāʿi, from bitāʿak! It's not mine, it's yours! 3. To ask who it is: bitāʿ mīn? · btāʿit mīn? · btūʿ mīn? 4. Never with kinship names: ummi, aḫūya, mirāti, not ... bitaʿti». With many common names the two forms are possible: kitābi = il-kitāb bitāʿi. In conversation bitāʿ is more frequent; in the curated writing and in the affective words one prefers the suffix. Other uses of bitāʿ. bitāʿ + name also indicates the name of... bitāʿ il-fūl The seller of fūl»; bitāʿ ʿašara ginēh From about ten pounds. 5. Family Egyptian Transliteration Translation ⁧أبويا⁩ · ⁧أب⁩ abb · abūya (bāba) father · my father (dad) ⁧أمي⁩ · ⁧أم⁩ umm · ummi (māma) mother · my mother (mom) ⁧أخويا⁩ · ⁧أخ⁩ aḫḫ · aḫūya brother · my brother ⁧أختي⁩ · ⁧أخت⁩ uḫt · uḫti sister · my sister ⁧بنت⁩ · ⁧ابن⁩ ibn · bint child · daughter ⁧ولاد⁩ · ⁧عيال⁩ ʿiyāl · wlād children, children ⁧مرات⁩ · ⁧جوز⁩ gōz · mirāt husband · wife (of) ⁧عمة⁩ · ⁧عم⁩ ʿamm · ʿamma Uncle Aunt (brother and sister of the father) ⁧خالة⁩ · ⁧خال⁩ ḫāl · ḫāla Uncle Aunt (brother and sister of the mother) ⁧جدة⁩ · ⁧جد⁩ gidd · gidda (giddu · tēta) Grandpa · Grandma ⁧بنت⁩ · ⁧ابن عمي⁩ ⁧خالتي⁩ ibn ʿammi · bint ḫālti my cousin (son of my father's uncle) · my cousin (daughter of the mother's aunt) ⁧حماة⁩ · ⁧حما⁩ ḥama · ḥamā father-in-law · mother-in-law ⁧قرايب⁩ ʾarāyib The cousin doesn't exist. Arabic does not have a word for "cousin": it is said of whom he is a son. ibn ʿammi, ibn ḫāli, ibn ʿammiti, ibn ḫālti They're four different people. mirāt "Wife" is used with a complement: mirāti, mirāt Ḥusām. For the sake of the lady alone, it is said that she is-sitt or madām. il-ḥagga is a respectful way to talk about your wife or an elderly lady (Lett. "He who made the pilgrimage"). 6. Dialogue 2 · The forgotten bag The shop of ʿAmm Fatḥi, in Milan. Luca's coming back for something. Egyptian Transliteration Translation ⁧لوكا: مساء الخير يا عم فتحي! نسيت شنطتي هنا امبارح؟⁩ Lūka: masāʾ il-ḫēr ya ʿAmm Fatḥi! nisīt šanṭiti hina mbāriḥ? Good evening. ʿAmm Fatḥi! title: At the restaurant and bar: ʿāyiz, lāzim, mumkin
text: Lesson overview Eating and drinking are the heart of Egyptian social life: it is ordered, tasted, commented, and in the end it is litigated to pay the bill. In this unity learn the three words that hold the daily conversation: ʿāyiz "I want to', lāzim "We need to, we need to, we need to, we can, I can, with their denials" (miš ʿāyiz, miš lāzim, but- yinfaʿš) and with nifsis I want to be. You also learn how to order at the restaurant and coffee, ask for coffee as you want (sāda, mazbūṭ, ziyāda) and to know the most common Egyptian dishes. Six weeks, in parallel with B1-20, the Test B1.3 and B1-21. Item Details Code EGY-08 Level B1 · EGY track (Egyptian Cairo) Prerequisites EGY-07 Estimated time 8–9 hours · six weeks (weeks 137–142), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian conversation partner; optional: the menu of an Egyptian restaurant (also online) Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. express wishes with ʿāyiz and nifsis, to the present and past (kunt ʿāyiz); 2. to express needs with lāzim and lack of need with miš lāzim, without confusing it with the ban; 3. ask and give permission with mumkin, yinfaʿ, ma-yinfaʿš; 4. order at the restaurant and coffee, with special requests (no onion, little sugar), and pay; 5. recognize the most common Egyptian dishes and drinks. Six-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). title: Practical problems: pharmacy, telephone, home, office
text: Lesson overview Luca is in Cairo for the summer course and lives again in the palace of ʿAmm Aḥmad, the goalkeeper who knows from the previous summer: ʿAmm Aḥmad Found him a small furnished apartment on the fourth floor. The days are full of lessons and discoveries, but also of small problems: a cold, bad air conditioning, internet that does not go, a line in an office, a wrong order. In this unit you learn to explain a malaise in the pharmacy, buy a SIM card and an internet package, ask for a repair, get away with it in an office and complain politely, in Egyptian. title: Opinions, TV series and authentic listening
text: Lesson overview The last unit of the Egyptian track takes you out of the built dialogues: learn to say what you think (ana šāyif Inn..., fi raʾyi...), whether or not to agree with the vivacity typical of an Egyptian discussion (laʾ ṭabʿan!, maʿāk miyya fi l-miyya), to talk about television series and movies, and above all to listen to the real Egyptian: fast, full of words that fill (yaʿni, ʾaṣdi, i-muhimm), contractions and jokes. Egyptian series and films are known all over the Arab world: they are also the most pleasant way to continue learning after this volume. Seven weeks, in parallel with INT-01INT-02, the Test B1.4 and B1-24. Item Details Code EGY-10 Level B1 · EGY track (Egyptian Cairo) Prerequisites EGY-09 Estimated time 10–11 hours · seven weeks (weeks 149–155), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks Materials This unit, a tutor or Egyptian conversation partner, an Egyptian series or film with Arabic subtitles (Appendix C) Targets. At the end of the unit you know: 1. express and motivate an opinion in Egyptian, and agree or disagree with gradations; 2. tell the plot of a movie or episode and say what you liked and what not; 3. recognizing and using the main words-signal of speech (yaʿni, ʾaṣdi, ʿala fikra, il-muhimm, ṭab, bass); 4. to understand the quick Egyptian in its most frequent phenomena (contractions, vocal falls, short forms); 5. follow an authentic scene of a series with a method in four stages. Seven-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week). The fast Egyptian In the quick talk of the series many words are shortened. Recognizing these forms is half of the work. Full form Quick form Translation ana ʾult lu ʾult-illu · ʾultillu I told him. ma-ʿaraftiš ma-ʿraftiš I did not know ʿalašān ʿašān · ʿalšān why, for ana ʿāyiz arūḥ ʿāyiz arūḥ · ʿayz arūḥ I want to go. il-ḥāga of il-ḥagādi This thing. inta bitiʿmil ēh? btiʿmil ēh? What are you doing? ḥa-aʿmil ḥaʿmil · haʿmil I'll do ēh From? ēda? What is it? ana miš ʿārif maʿrafš I don't know. Other phenomena. Short vowels that are not accented fall: kitīr → ktīr, simiʿt → smiʿt. The ḥa- of the future often becomes ha-. Foreign words are everywhere (mobāyl, laptop, uber, story): it's not a problem, it's contemporary Egyptian. 8. Listening to the authentic Egyptian What to choose. To begin with: a recent Egyptian series or film, with subtitles in Arabic (not in English), and scenes of daily dialogue (family, friends, work). Classic black and white films (the 1950s and 1960s, with actresses and actors like Fātin Ḥamāma) have a slower and clearer Egyptian, and are still very loved. See Appendix C for platforms and resources. The method in four stages (for a scene of 2–3 minutes). 1. Look without stopping, with Arab subtitles. Who am I, where am I, what's going on? Write three words key. 2. Look again, sentence by sentence. Stop after every line, read the subtitle, repeat aloud. Note the new words and words-signal (section 5). 3. Look without subtitles. Now you understand more: mark in percentage how much (like Luke: 70% with 50% without). 4. Shadowing and summarized. Repeat three lines imitating rhythm and intonation; then tells the scene in Egyptian in One minute. How much? One scene a day, fifteen minutes, is worth more than one whole movie once a month. It's about the same scene after a week: you'll see how much better listening has been. 9. Pronunciation The emphasis on opinion. In Egyptian the emphasis is placed stretching and raising the voice on the important word: from ḥilw ʾaaawi! · laʾ ṭabʿaaan! · miyya fi l-miyya! Imitates the tutor: it is part of the meaning. The rhetorical questions. izzāy yaʿni?! What would it be like?!! and mumill?! They are said with a very high pitch and then comes down suddenly: it is astonishment, not a real question. 10.
